exam.title: Importação externa - MichalisKampouridis/security-plus-study
exam.notes: Third-party questions from https://github.com/MichalisKampouridis/security-plus-study @ a65fd4378d2fad4db5c2fb183d3d0306160e403c (license: NOASSERTION, registry status: approved). All 476 items reviewed and approved by SME (needs_review=false, explanation_source=editor).

questions.question: A security architect is redesigning an enterprise network so that no user or device is implicitly trusted based on network location. Every access request is evaluated by a policy engine and a policy administrator before a policy enforcement point grants access to a resource. Which security model is being implemented?

options.text: Perimeter-based security architecture relying on trusted internal network zones

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Zero Trust removes implicit trust based on network location: every request is evaluated in the control plane by the policy engine and policy administrator and then enforced by a policy enforcement point in the data plane. Network segmentation (A) is only one technique that can support Zero Trust, not the overall model. A perimeter-based architecture (C) is exactly the opposite, because it trusts internal zones by default. Defense in depth (D) is a layering philosophy and does not define the policy engine/administrator/enforcement point model.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Policy engine/administrator plus enforcement point with no implicit trust describes Zero Trust; key verified. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization wants to ensure that cryptographic keys used for full-disk encryption are generated and stored in tamper-resistant hardware on both end-user laptops and centralized data center servers. Which TWO technologies should the organization use to meet this requirement? (Choose TWO.)
questions.justification: A TPM is a chip embedded in end-user devices such as laptops that securely generates and stores encryption keys, supporting full-disk encryption. An HSM is a dedicated hardware appliance used in data centers to generate, store, and manage cryptographic keys at scale. Steganography (B), data masking (D), and tokenization (E) are obfuscation techniques that hide or substitute data values rather than securely storing cryptographic keys in hardware.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - TPM protects keys on endpoints and HSM in data centers; distractors are obfuscation techniques.

questions.question: A company installs security cameras at building entrances that are monitored 24/7 by a security operations team. Which category of control does this represent?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Cameras protecting building entrances are a physical control: tangible measures that protect facilities, like fences, locks and guards. Technical controls (B) are implemented by systems and software such as firewalls, encryption or ACLs that protect data. Operational controls (C) are procedures carried out by people day to day, such as guard patrols or awareness training. Managerial controls (D) are policies and risk decisions made by leadership. Even though cameras are electronic, CompTIA classifies them as physical because they protect a physical space.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Monitored cameras protecting facility entrances are a physical control category. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization posts highly visible signs at the perimeter of its data center stating that the area is under video surveillance and that trespassers will be prosecuted. Which type of control does this BEST represent?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Visible warning signs discourage an intruder from attempting the action at all, which is a deterrent control. Corrective controls (B) act after an incident to restore systems or limit damage, such as restoring from backup. Detective controls (C) identify that an event already happened, such as reviewing footage after a break-in; the cameras may be detective, but the sign itself is not. Compensating controls (D) are alternative safeguards used when a primary control cannot be implemented, which is not described here.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Warning signage is the textbook deterrent control. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A retail store installs security cameras at each entrance. The footage is actively monitored in real time by a guard who can dispatch staff if suspicious activity is observed. Which TWO categories or types BEST describe this control? (Choose TWO.)
questions.justification:
The cameras themselves are physical hardware deployed to protect a physical space, making this a physical control. Because the footage is actively monitored and used to identify and respond to suspicious activity, it also functions as a detective control. Preventive (C) controls stop an action before it occurs, such as a locked door, which is not the camera's role. Managerial (D) controls are policy and risk decisions made by leadership, and directive (E) controls are mandated procedures β€” neither describes a camera system itself.

CompTIA logic: Students sometimes select 'Preventive' because a visibly monitored camera might deter an attack, but that deterrence is a side effect, not the control's classification. CompTIA classifies actively monitored cameras as physical plus detective because their primary function is identifying activity, not blocking it.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Actively monitored cameras are physical (category) and detective (type).

questions.question:
A hospital relies on a legacy radiology imaging system that runs on an operating system the vendor no longer supports with security patches. Replacing the system is not financially feasible for at least two years. The security team isolates the system on its own VLAN with strict firewall rules that allow only the minimum necessary traffic to and from a small number of authorized workstations.

The VLAN isolation and restrictive firewall rules implemented around the unpatchable system are an example of which type of control?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Because the primary control (vendor patching) cannot be applied, VLAN isolation and restrictive firewall rules act as an alternative safeguard that reduces risk: a compensating control. Corrective controls (A) act after an incident to restore or repair systems. Detective controls (C) identify activity that has already occurred rather than reducing exposure. Preventive (D) is tempting because segmentation blocks traffic, but CompTIA uses "compensating" when a measure substitutes for a control that cannot be implemented, which is the key cue in the scenario.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Network isolation substituting for unavailable patches is a compensating control. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: Which of the following activities is BEST classified as an operational control?

options.text: Configuring a host-based firewall to block unauthorized inbound traffic
Installing a badge reader on the server room door
Approving an enterprise-wide risk management policy at the board level
Requiring all employees to complete annual security awareness training

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Operational controls are carried out primarily by people as part of day-to-day activities, and a recurring security awareness training program fits that definition. Configuring a host-based firewall (A) is a technical control enforced by software. A badge reader on a door (B) is a physical control. Board approval of a risk management policy (C) is a managerial control, because it is a governance and risk decision made by leadership rather than an activity performed by staff.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Recurring people-driven security awareness training is an operational control. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A file transfer system calculates a cryptographic hash of each file before it is sent and again after it is received, comparing the two values to ensure the file was not altered in transit. Which principle of the CIA triad does this process primarily support?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Hashing the file before sending and after receipt and comparing the digests proves the content was not altered, which is integrity. Availability (A) concerns keeping systems and data accessible when needed. Confidentiality (C) concerns preventing unauthorized disclosure, which a hash comparison does not provide because the file is not encrypted. Non-repudiation (D) prevents a sender from denying an action and requires a digital signature bound to a private key, not a plain hash comparison.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Comparing hashes before and after transfer verifies integrity. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A company requires that all financial transfer approval emails be digitally signed using the sender's private key. If a finance manager later denies having approved a transfer, the company can use the digital signature to prove the manager did, in fact, send the approval. Which security concept does this scenario illustrate?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. A digital signature created with the sender's private key binds the approval cryptographically to that individual, so the manager cannot credibly deny sending it: non-repudiation. Authorization (A) defines what an authenticated user is allowed to do. Accounting (B) logs user actions for auditing, but logs alone do not provide cryptographic proof of origin. Confidentiality (C) keeps the email contents secret and does not prove who sent it.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A private-key digital signature proving the approver sent the message is non-repudiation. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: When a user logs into a corporate VPN, the system verifies the user's username and password, checks which network resources that user is permitted to access, and records the time, duration, and resources accessed during the session in a log. Which TWO components of the AAA framework are represented by checking permitted resources and logging session details? (Choose TWO.)
questions.justification: Authorization determines which resources an authenticated user is permitted to access, matching the description of checking permitted resources. Accounting records what a user did during a session β€” the time, duration, and resources accessed β€” for auditing purposes. Authentication (A) refers to verifying the username and password, which is described but is not one of the two components asked about. Availability (D) and non-repudiation (E) are unrelated concepts outside the AAA framework.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Checking permitted resources is authorization; logging session details is accounting.

questions.question: In a Zero Trust architecture, a component continuously evaluates contextual signals such as user identity, device health, and location to make a real-time decision about whether to grant access to a resource, and then instructs another component to allow or block the connection. Which Zero Trust component makes this access decision?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. The policy engine, in the control plane, evaluates signals such as identity, device health and location and decides whether access is granted, then the policy administrator/enforcement point act on it. The policy enforcement point (A) sits in the data plane and only allows or blocks the connection based on the decision. The subject (B) is the user or system requesting access. An implicit trust zone (D) is the legacy concept Zero Trust tries to eliminate, not a decision-making component.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - The policy engine is the Zero Trust component that makes the access decision. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: Before submitting a request to upgrade a critical database server's operating system, an administrator documents which applications depend on the server, how the upgrade could affect each one, and what risks the organization would face if those applications became unavailable. Which step of the change management process does this represent?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Identifying which applications depend on the server, how the upgrade could affect them and the business risk of downtime is impact analysis, performed before the change is approved. Maintenance window scheduling (A) decides when the change occurs, not its potential effects. Version control (B) tracks revisions of code, configurations and documentation over time. A backout plan (C) describes how to revert the change if it fails, which is a separate component of the change request.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Documenting dependencies and effects of a change before approval is impact analysis. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A systems administrator configures a host-based firewall so that only explicitly approved applications are permitted to establish outbound network connections; all other applications are blocked by default. Which technical implication of change management does this configuration represent?

options.text: Restricted activity enforcement via a software-defined policy engine

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Permitting only explicitly approved applications and blocking everything else by default is an allow list, one of the technical implications of change management in SY0-701. The option about a software-defined policy engine (A) is invented wording that does not describe this host firewall setting. Dependency mapping (C) documents relationships between systems and does not restrict network access. A deny list (D) does the opposite: it blocks specific known-bad items and allows everything else by default.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Default-deny with explicitly approved applications is an allow list. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A network administrator successfully completes a firewall configuration change and confirms connectivity is working. What should the administrator do NEXT according to change management best practices?

options.text: Notify only senior management and skip technical documentation updates
Open a new change request for any related improvements discovered during the change
Update all network diagrams and configuration documentation to reflect the change
Close the change ticket immediately since the change succeeded

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Change management requires updating network diagrams, configuration records and procedures after a change so documentation reflects reality for future troubleshooting, audits and impact analysis. Notifying only management and skipping documentation (A) violates the process. Opening a new change request for improvements (B) may happen later but does not complete the current change. Closing the ticket immediately (D) without updating records leaves documentation out of date and creates operational and audit risk.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - After a successful change, documentation and diagrams must be updated. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A CISO requires that all laptops use a U.S. federal standard symmetric encryption algorithm supporting key lengths of 128, 192, or 256 bits to protect data at rest. Which algorithm should be selected?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. AES is the NIST-approved symmetric block cipher and supports 128-, 192- and 256-bit keys, making it the standard choice for encrypting laptop data at rest. SHA-256 (A) is a hashing algorithm and cannot encrypt or decrypt data. 3DES (C) is a legacy symmetric cipher that is deprecated and does not offer those key lengths. RSA (D) is an asymmetric algorithm used for key exchange and signatures, not efficient bulk encryption of disks.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - AES is the NIST symmetric standard with 128/192/256-bit keys. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: Two parties who have never communicated before need to securely agree on a shared secret key over an untrusted network, without ever transmitting the key itself in plaintext. Which type of cryptography is BEST suited to establish this shared secret?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Asymmetric (public key) cryptography, such as Diffie-Hellman or RSA key exchange, lets two parties with no prior relationship derive or exchange a shared secret without ever sending it in plaintext. Hashing (A) is a one-way function and cannot establish a shared key. Data masking (B) hides data values for display or testing and is unrelated to key exchange. Symmetric encryption (D) requires both parties to already share the same key, which is precisely the problem to be solved.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Establishing a shared secret between strangers over an untrusted network requires asymmetric cryptography (e.g., Diffie-Hellman/RSA). - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question:
A developer is designing a system to store user passwords. Two users on the system happen to choose the identical password, 'Summer2024!'. The developer wants to ensure that even though both users chose the same password, their stored password values are completely different, so that an attacker who steals the password database cannot use a precomputed table of common password hashes to quickly crack either account.

Which technique should the developer apply before hashing each user's password to achieve this goal?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Salting adds a unique random value to each password before hashing, so identical passwords produce different stored hashes and precomputed rainbow tables become useless. Tokenization (A) replaces sensitive values such as card numbers with tokens and is not used for password storage. Steganography (C) hides data inside other files. Key stretching (D) such as PBKDF2 or bcrypt slows each hash computation to resist brute force, but on its own does not make identical passwords produce different values.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A unique salt per password makes identical passwords hash differently and defeats rainbow tables. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization is building a public key infrastructure to issue certificates to internal web servers. Which TWO of the following are responsible for issuing and validating the trustworthiness of digital certificates within this PKI? (Choose TWO.)
questions.justification: A certificate authority (CA) issues digital certificates and forms the root of trust within a PKI, vouching for the identity bound to a public key. An OCSP responder allows relying parties to check, in real time, whether a previously issued certificate has been revoked, helping validate its current trustworthiness. A data masking engine (C) and tokenization vault (D) are data protection tools unrelated to certificate issuance. A steganography tool (E) hides data inside other files and is unrelated to PKI.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - CA issues certificates and OCSP responder validates revocation status.

questions.question: A relying party needs to determine whether a specific TLS certificate presented by a web server has been revoked before the connection is trusted. The organization wants this check to happen in near real time with minimal delay, rather than the client downloading and searching a large, periodically updated list of all revoked certificates. Which method BEST meets this requirement?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. OCSP lets the client query a responder about one specific certificate and receive a good/revoked/unknown answer in near real time, without downloading a large list. A CSR (A) is the request sent to a CA to obtain a certificate and is not a revocation check. A CRL (B) is a periodically published list of all revoked certificates that the client must download and search, which is exactly what the organization wants to avoid. A self-signed certificate (C) is not issued by a trusted CA and has nothing to do with revocation checking.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - OCSP provides near-real-time revocation checks for a single certificate, unlike a CRL. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A developer needs to implement a cryptographic algorithm that uses a mathematically related public and private key pair, allowing the private key to be used for digital signatures while the public key, distributed openly, can verify those signatures. Which of the following algorithms is designed for this purpose?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. RSA is an asymmetric algorithm with a mathematically related key pair: the private key signs and the openly distributed public key verifies the signature. AES (A) and ChaCha20 (B) are symmetric ciphers that use one shared secret key for both encryption and decryption, so they cannot provide public verification of signatures. SHA-256 (C) is a hashing algorithm; it is used inside signature schemes to create the digest but has no key pair of its own.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - RSA is the asymmetric algorithm used for digital signatures with a public/private key pair. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization stations a uniformed guard at the main entrance who checks employee badges before allowing anyone into the building. From a control category standpoint, the guard's badge check is BEST classified as a:

options.text: Operational control implemented entirely in software

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. A guard manually checking badges at a door is a tangible measure restricting physical access, so its category is physical. Option A is wrong because a human guard is not implemented in software, and operational controls are not software-based by definition. Technical controls (B) are enforced by hardware or software configuration, such as ACLs or encryption. Managerial controls (C) are leadership policy and risk decisions, such as approving a guard program, not the act of checking badges.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A guard checking badges is a physical control category. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are examples of detective controls? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Reviewing security camera footage after a break-in to identify the intruder
Installing a fence around the perimeter of a facility
Analyzing audit logs to identify unauthorized login attempts that already occurred
Configuring a firewall rule to block traffic before it reaches a server
Encrypting a hard drive so stolen data cannot be read

questions.justification:
Detective controls identify that an adverse event has already occurred, such as reviewing camera footage after a break-in or analyzing audit logs to find unauthorized login attempts that already happened. A fence (B) is a preventive/physical control that stops access before it happens. A firewall rule blocking traffic (D) is a preventive control because it stops the event before it occurs. Encrypting a hard drive (E) is a preventive control that protects data confidentiality in advance, not a detection mechanism.

CompTIA logic: The key distinguishing word for detective controls is 'after' β€” they identify or record events that have already taken place, whereas preventive controls act 'before' an event to stop it from happening at all.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Reviewing footage and analyzing logs after the fact are detective controls.

questions.question: An organization cannot implement MFA on a critical legacy system due to technical incompatibility. The security team adds manual access review processes and enhanced monitoring specific to that system. This measure is BEST described as a:
questions.justification: A compensating control is an alternative safeguard put in place when a required primary control cannot be implemented, providing a comparable level of risk reduction. Here, MFA cannot be applied, so enhanced monitoring and manual review substitute for it. A corrective control (A) acts after an incident to restore systems. A detective control (C) identifies events that have already occurred. A directive control (D) mandates required behavior through policies or procedures.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Monitoring and manual reviews substituting for MFA that cannot be deployed are compensating controls.

questions.question: An organization publishes a formal policy requiring all employees to complete annual security awareness training and to report lost devices within one hour of discovery. This policy itself functions as which type of control?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. A formal policy that mandates behavior, such as completing training and reporting lost devices, is a directive control. A physical control (B) is a tangible barrier or device such as a lock or fence, not a written requirement. A compensating control (C) substitutes for a primary control that cannot be implemented, which is not the case here. A detective control (D) identifies that a violation or event has already occurred rather than directing behavior in advance.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A written policy mandating behavior is a directive control. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a technical security control?

options.text: A fence surrounding the building's perimeter
A risk assessment conducted annually by the security team
An access control list (ACL) on a router that blocks traffic from a specific IP range
A policy requiring new hires to sign an acceptable use agreement

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. An ACL on a router is enforced by device configuration and software, which makes it a technical control. A perimeter fence (A) is a physical control. An annual risk assessment (B) is a managerial activity used to guide decisions. A policy requiring new hires to sign an acceptable use agreement (D) is a managerial/administrative control that relies on people following policy rather than on technology enforcing it.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A router ACL is a technical control. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are examples of preventive controls? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Requiring multifactor authentication before granting access to a VPN
Reviewing intrusion detection system alerts each morning
Locking a laptop in a cable lock to a desk
Generating a weekly report of failed login attempts

questions.justification: Preventive controls stop an unwanted action before it can occur, such as requiring MFA before granting VPN access or physically securing a laptop with a cable lock so it cannot be easily stolen. Reviewing IDS alerts (B) and generating a report of failed logins (E) are detective activities because they identify events that have already happened. A lessons-learned meeting (D) is part of the incident response process that occurs after an incident, related to corrective improvements rather than prevention of the original event.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - MFA before VPN access and a cable lock both stop the event before it happens (preventive).

questions.question: An organization encrypts customer Social Security numbers stored in its database so that even if an attacker gains access to the raw database files, the values cannot be read without the decryption key. This control primarily supports which principle of the CIA triad?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Encrypting SSNs at rest prevents unauthorized disclosure even if the raw database files are stolen, which is confidentiality. Availability (A) keeps systems and data accessible when needed and is not the goal of encryption. Integrity (C) ensures data has not been altered and is usually verified with hashing or signatures. Non-repudiation (D) prevents someone from denying an action and is not part of the CIA triad.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Encrypting data at rest protects confidentiality. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An e-commerce company deploys its web application across multiple availability zones, configures automatic failover, and load-balances traffic between redundant servers. These measures are primarily intended to support which principle of the CIA triad?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Multiple availability zones, automatic failover and load balancing keep the application reachable despite failures, which supports availability. Accounting (A) belongs to the AAA framework and records user activity, not uptime. Integrity (B) protects data from unauthorized modification. Confidentiality (C) protects data from unauthorized disclosure. Neither integrity nor confidentiality is the main purpose of redundant infrastructure. Key takeaway: the details in this scenario point to Availability.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Redundancy, failover and load balancing support availability. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A user types their username and password into a corporate login portal. The system verifies the credentials, grants the user access only to the file shares assigned to their department, and records the date, time, and resources accessed in a log for later review. Which TWO of the following AAA components are demonstrated in this scenario? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Authentication β€” verifying the username and password
Accounting β€” logging the date, time, and resources accessed
Authorization β€” encrypting the file shares
Identification β€” granting access only to assigned file shares
Non-repudiation β€” recording the user's IP address

questions.justification:
Authentication is the process of verifying that the user is who they claim to be, demonstrated by checking the username and password. Accounting is the process of recording user activity for later review, demonstrated by logging the date, time, and resources accessed. Option C mislabels authorization, which is determining what an authenticated user is permitted to do (granting access to assigned file shares), not encryption. Option D mislabels authorization as identification; identification is simply claiming an identity (entering the username), not the access decision. Option E describes a logging detail, not a formal AAA component on its own.

CompTIA logic: Authorization is granting access to the file shares assigned to the user's department β€” this is the part of the scenario that option C and D incorrectly describe. Since the question asks for the TWO components that are clearly and correctly demonstrated, authentication and accounting are the safest, unambiguous choices.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Verifying credentials is authentication and logging activity is accounting; other options mislabel components.

questions.question: A contractor attempts to open a confidential file on a shared drive. The system successfully verifies the contractor's smart card and PIN, but then denies access to the file because the contractor's account is not a member of the group assigned to that folder. Which statement BEST describes what occurred?
tags: AAA Framework - Authentication vs Authorization vs Accounting

options.text: Accounting failed, preventing authentication from completing

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. The smart card and PIN verification succeeded, so authentication worked; the denial happened because the account lacks the required group membership, which is an authorization failure. Option A is wrong because accounting only records events and never blocks authentication. Option B reverses the facts: authentication clearly succeeded. Option D is wrong because the identity was verified successfully; only the permission check failed.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Smart card plus PIN succeeded (authentication) but group membership denied access (authorization failure). - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: When a new employee starts at a company, the HR department issues them a unique employee ID number and a corresponding username that will be used across all internal systems. This act of assigning a unique username is BEST described as:
questions.justification: Identification is the process of establishing a unique identifier (such as a username) that represents an individual within a system, which is the first step before any verification occurs. Authentication (B) is the subsequent process of proving that identity, typically with a password, token, or biometric. Authorization (C) determines what the identified and authenticated user is permitted to do. Federation (D) refers to extending authentication and authorization across organizational boundaries using a trusted third party, unrelated to assigning an initial username.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Assigning a unique username is identification.

questions.question: Which statement BEST summarizes the core philosophy of a Zero Trust security model?

options.text: Trust is granted permanently once a user successfully authenticates at the start of the day
Never trust, always verify β€” every access request must be authenticated and authorized regardless of its origin
Perimeter firewalls are sufficient to protect all internal resources without further verification
Trust all devices and users on the internal network by default, and verify only external connections

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Zero Trust is summarized as "never trust, always verify": every access request is authenticated and authorized regardless of where it originates. Option A is wrong because Zero Trust requires continuous verification rather than permanent trust after one login. Option C describes perimeter-only security, which Zero Trust replaces because threats can bypass or originate inside the perimeter. Option D describes the traditional implicit-trust internal network, the exact opposite of Zero Trust.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - "Never trust, always verify" is the Zero Trust philosophy. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: In a Zero Trust architecture, the control plane and data plane perform distinct functions. Which TWO of the following components belong to the control plane? (Choose TWO.)
tags: Zero Trust - Control Plane vs Data Plane
questions.justification:
The control plane in a Zero Trust architecture is responsible for deciding whether to grant access, and consists of the policy engine, which evaluates access requests against policy, and the policy administrator, which executes that decision by establishing or terminating the communication path. The policy enforcement point (C) resides in the data plane and is the component that actually allows or blocks the connection based on the control plane's decision. The subject (D) and the resource (E) are the entities involved in the access request itself, not control-plane decision-making components.

CompTIA logic: The policy enforcement point is the most commonly confused component because its name sounds like a decision-maker. CompTIA's model places decision-making (policy engine and policy administrator) in the control plane, while the policy enforcement point sits in the data plane and simply carries out the decision by permitting or blocking traffic.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Policy engine and policy administrator are control-plane components.

questions.question: A security team deploys a server that appears to host an outdated, vulnerable database application, but it contains no real data and exists solely to attract and observe attacker behavior. This server is an example of a:
questions.justification: A honeypot is a decoy system designed to appear as an attractive target in order to lure attackers, allowing defenders to study their tactics and divert them from real production systems. A jump server (B) is a hardened intermediary host used by legitimate administrators to access other systems. A bastion host (C) is a hardened server exposed to untrusted networks that provides a controlled entry point. A screened subnet (D) is a network architecture concept (formerly called a DMZ), not a decoy system.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A decoy system with no real data designed to attract attackers is a honeypot.

questions.question: A security team creates a fake administrator account named 'svc_backup_admin' with a password stored in a configuration file that is never used by any legitimate process. If this account is ever used to log in, an alert is immediately triggered. This fake credential is an example of a:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. A honeytoken is fake data, such as an unused credential or API key, planted so that any use of it reveals unauthorized access. A honeynet (A) is an entire decoy network of honeypots. A sinkhole (B) redirects malicious traffic, such as DNS requests for known-bad domains, to a controlled destination. A honeyfile (D) is a decoy document that alerts when opened; related, but the scenario describes a fake account credential, not a file.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A fake credential that alerts when used is a honeytoken. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A company installs a row of sturdy, closely spaced concrete posts along the sidewalk in front of its main entrance. The primary purpose of these posts is to:

options.text: Detect unauthorized access attempts and trigger an alarm
Provide lighting for the entrance area at night
Prevent vehicles from ramming or driving into the building
Authenticate visitors before they enter the lobby

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Sturdy, closely spaced concrete posts are bollards, a physical barrier that prevents vehicles from ramming or driving into the building entrance. They have no sensors and do not detect or alarm (A). They are not lighting fixtures (B), although lighting is another physical control. They do not verify identities (D); authentication of visitors is done by guards, badges or access control vestibules.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Bollards prevent vehicle ramming; the stem is easy. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are examples of physical security controls used to protect a data center? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: A mantrap that allows only one person to pass through at a time after badge verification
An access control list on a database limiting which accounts can read customer records
Motion-activated lighting around the building perimeter
A software firewall rule blocking inbound traffic on port 23
A policy requiring quarterly access reviews

questions.justification: A mantrap is a physical access control consisting of a small enclosed space with two interlocking doors that prevents more than one person from entering at a time, often paired with badge or biometric verification. Perimeter lighting is also a physical control that improves visibility and deters intruders. A database access control list (B) and a software firewall rule (D) are technical controls implemented through software. A policy requiring access reviews (E) is a managerial/administrative control, not a physical one.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Mantrap and perimeter lighting are physical controls; ACLs/firewall rules are technical and policy is managerial.

questions.question: An organization protects a sensitive database with the following layers: a perimeter firewall, a network intrusion prevention system, host-based antivirus on the database server, encryption of data at rest, and strict database-level access controls. If an attacker successfully bypasses the perimeter firewall, which security principle ensures the attacker still faces additional obstacles before reaching the data?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Defense in depth layers multiple independent controls (firewall, IPS, host antivirus, encryption, database access controls) so that bypassing one still leaves others in place. A single point of failure (A) is a weakness where one component's failure breaks everything, the opposite of layering. Security through obscurity (B) relies on hiding details and is weak on its own. Implicit deny (C) is a specific access control rule (deny anything not explicitly allowed), not the overarching layering principle.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Layered independent controls describe defense in depth. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A building manager installs cameras at all entry points recording continuously to a 30-day archive. After a physical intrusion is discovered, the security team reviews the footage to identify the intruder. What is the PRIMARY control type classification of this camera recording system?
tags: Physical Security - Video Surveillance as Detective Control
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Recorded footage reviewed after an intrusion identifies what happened and who did it, so the camera system is primarily a detective control. A preventive control (A) stops an action before it occurs, such as a locked door. A deterrent control (B) discourages attempts; visible cameras can deter, but that is a secondary effect. A corrective control (D) acts after an incident to restore systems or limit further damage.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Recording cameras reviewed after an intrusion are primarily detective. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A security team compares its organization's current access control practices against the requirements outlined in a target security framework, documenting where current practices fall short so that remediation can be planned. This activity is BEST described as a:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. A gap analysis compares the current state with a desired or required state (such as a framework) and documents the shortfalls to plan remediation. A tabletop exercise (B) is a discussion-based incident simulation. A penetration test (C) actively exploits technical vulnerabilities rather than comparing practices with a standard. A vulnerability scan (D) is an automated technical assessment for known weaknesses, not a documented comparison against framework requirements.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Comparing current practices to a target framework is a gap analysis. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An employee logs into a banking application by entering a password and then scanning their fingerprint on their phone. A security analyst is asked whether this constitutes true multifactor authentication. Which of the following is the BEST response?

options.text: No, because both steps occur on the same device, so they count as only one factor
Yes, because the password represents 'something you know' and the fingerprint represents 'something you are,' which are two different factor categories
Yes, but only because the fingerprint scan happens after the password, making it a corrective control
No, because a fingerprint is considered 'something you have,' the same category as a password

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. MFA requires factors from different categories; a password is something you know and a fingerprint is something you are, so this is true multifactor authentication. Option A is wrong because MFA depends on factor categories, not on how many devices are used. Option C wrongly applies the term "corrective control" to an authentication factor. Option D is wrong because a fingerprint is something you are, and a password is something you know, not something you have.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Password (know) plus fingerprint (are) is true MFA even on the same device. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a formal change management process within an organization?
tags: Change Management - Purpose of the Process

options.text: To replace the need for testing changes before deployment
To prevent any changes to production systems from ever occurring
To automatically deploy all requested changes without review to save time
To ensure changes to systems are reviewed, approved, and documented in order to minimize unintended disruptions

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Formal change management ensures that changes are reviewed, tested, approved and documented to minimize unintended outages and security issues. It does not replace testing (A); testing results are normally required in the change request. It does not prevent all changes (B); it controls how they happen. It does not deploy changes automatically without review (C), which would defeat its purpose.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Change management ensures changes are reviewed, approved and documented to minimize disruption. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: As part of a change request to update firewall firmware, the change documentation includes a section describing the exact steps to restore the firewall to its previous firmware version and configuration if the update causes connectivity issues. This section is known as the:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. A backout plan documents the exact steps to revert a change and restore the previous known-good state if the change causes problems. A memorandum of understanding (A) records a general intent to cooperate between parties. A risk register (B) tracks identified organizational risks, not a reversal procedure. A service level agreement (D) defines expected service performance between a provider and customer.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Steps to revert to the previous configuration form the backout plan. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: When is the MOST appropriate time to schedule a significant firmware upgrade to a core network switch that will require a brief network outage?

options.text: During peak business hours so all technical staff are available to assist
During a scheduled maintenance window when user activity is at its lowest
Immediately upon approval to minimize the vulnerability exposure window
Only after the vulnerability has already been actively exploited in the environment

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Maintenance windows are pre-scheduled periods of low user activity reserved for changes, which minimizes business impact if the upgrade causes problems. Doing the upgrade during peak hours (A) maximizes the number of affected users even if staff are available. Implementing immediately upon approval (C) ignores the timing controls that change management uses to limit disruption. Waiting until the vulnerability is actively exploited (D) leaves a known exposure open far longer than necessary.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Disruptive changes belong in a scheduled low-usage maintenance window. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: Before applying a major application update to production servers, a development team deploys the update to an isolated environment that mirrors production but has no connection to live customer data, allowing them to validate the update without risk. This isolated environment is known as a:
tags: Change Management - Testing in a Sandbox
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. A sandbox is an isolated environment that mirrors production without touching live data, so changes can be validated safely before deployment. A jump server (A) is a hardened intermediary host administrators use to reach other systems. A honeynet (B) is a decoy network used to study attackers, not to test legitimate updates. A screened subnet (C) is a network zone that exposes public services while protecting the internal network.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - An isolated production-like environment for validating changes is a sandbox/test environment. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: When submitting a request to a change advisory board for a significant configuration change to a production database server, which TWO of the following should typically be included in the documentation? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: An impact analysis describing which systems or users could be affected by the change
A backout plan describing how to revert the change if issues occur
A copy of the organization's annual financial statements
The personal home address of the engineer performing the change
A list of unrelated marketing campaigns scheduled for the same quarter

questions.justification: A well-documented change request should include an impact analysis identifying which systems, services, or users could be affected, and a backout plan describing how to revert the change if problems occur, allowing the change advisory board to assess risk and approve appropriately. Financial statements (C), an engineer's home address (D), and unrelated marketing campaigns (E) have no relevance to evaluating the technical and operational risk of a system change.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Impact analysis and backout plan belong in a change request; distractors are absurd.

questions.question:
An administrator, under pressure to fix a reported issue quickly, makes a configuration change directly on a production router without submitting a change request, without testing in a staging environment, and without documenting a backout plan. The change causes a widespread outage that takes several hours to diagnose because no one knew what had changed.

Which of the following BEST identifies the control failure that most directly contributed to the extended outage?
tags: Change Management - Consequences of Bypassing the Process

options.text: The administrator used a weak password to access the router
The administrator bypassed the change management process, so there was no documentation, testing, or backout plan to quickly identify and reverse the cause of the outage
The organization failed to encrypt data in transit on the router
The router's firmware was outdated, which is unrelated to the change management process

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. The outage was prolonged because the change bypassed change management: there was no request, no testing, no documentation and no backout plan, so no one knew what changed or how to revert it. A weak router password (A) is not described and did not cause the outage. Missing encryption of data in transit (C) has nothing to do with the configuration error. Outdated firmware (D) is irrelevant to an undocumented, untested manual change.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Bypassing change management left no record, testing or backout plan. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: Two parties need to establish a shared encryption key over an untrusted public network without any prior shared secret, each contributing private values while publicly exchanging other values. Which key exchange protocol accomplishes this?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Diffie-Hellman lets two parties each combine a private value with publicly exchanged values to derive the same shared secret, which an eavesdropper cannot compute. AES key wrapping (B) protects a key using another symmetric key that must already be shared. OCSP (C) checks certificate revocation status and does not establish keys. RSA key transport (D) has one party encrypt a key with the other's public key and send it, rather than both parties contributing values to derive it.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Diffie-Hellman derives a shared secret from exchanged public values without a prior secret. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A mobile developer needs asymmetric cryptography for device authentication but must minimize key sizes to reduce battery and processing overhead. Which approach provides equivalent security to RSA with significantly smaller key sizes?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Elliptic Curve Cryptography is asymmetric and provides security equivalent to RSA with far smaller keys, reducing CPU and battery use on mobile devices. SHA-512 (A) is a hash function, not an asymmetric algorithm. 3DES (B) is a legacy symmetric cipher and does not provide public/private key pairs. MD5 (C) is a broken hash function and cannot be used for asymmetric authentication.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - ECC offers RSA-equivalent security with much smaller keys, suitable for mobile devices. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization building an internal PKI needs to designate the trusted entity responsible for issuing, signing, and revoking digital certificates that will be trusted by all internal systems. Which PKI component fulfills this role?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. The Certificate Authority is the trusted entity that issues, signs and revokes certificates and forms the root of trust of the PKI. A policy enforcement point (A) is a Zero Trust data-plane component unrelated to PKI. A CRL (B) is a list of revoked certificates published by the CA, not the issuing entity. An OCSP responder (D) answers revocation-status queries but does not issue or sign end-entity certificates.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - The CA issues, signs and revokes certificates. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A web server administrator generates a key pair and needs to create a file containing the server's public key plus organizational identifying information to submit to a CA in order to receive a signed TLS certificate. What is this file called?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. A Certificate Signing Request contains the applicant's public key and identifying information and is submitted to the CA, which validates it and returns a signed certificate. An OCSP staple (B) is a cached revocation-status response the server presents during the TLS handshake. A CRL (C) is a list of revoked certificates. A private key export file (D) must never be sent to a CA; the private key stays on the server.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A CSR contains the public key and identity info sent to a CA. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A financial institution needs to generate, store, and manage cryptographic keys for its PKI in a tamper-evident, purpose-built hardware device that physically protects against key extraction even by administrators. Which solution BEST meets this requirement?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. A Hardware Security Module is a dedicated, tamper-resistant appliance for generating, storing and managing keys at enterprise scale, designed so keys cannot be extracted even by administrators. An encrypted USB drive (A) is portable storage, not a key management appliance. A TPM (B) is a chip embedded in an individual device for device-level keys such as BitLocker. A software-based key management system (C) lacks hardware-level tamper protection.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A tamper-resistant appliance for enterprise PKI key management is an HSM. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization wants BitLocker full-disk encryption keys stored in dedicated hardware permanently integrated into employee laptops that can also verify boot process integrity. Which component should be used?

options.text: Software key store in the OS keychain

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. A TPM is a chip built into the laptop motherboard that securely stores BitLocker keys and measures the boot process to detect tampering. A smart card reader (A) reads an external authentication token and is not permanently integrated key storage. A software key store (B) offers no hardware tamper protection. An HSM (D) is a standalone appliance or card used in data centers, not a chip embedded in each laptop.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - TPM is the motherboard chip storing BitLocker keys and measuring boot integrity. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A company configures its web servers to use ephemeral Diffie-Hellman key exchanges, generating a new temporary key pair for every TLS session rather than reusing a long-term key. This configuration ensures that if the server's long-term private key is later compromised, past recorded sessions cannot be decrypted. This property is known as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Perfect forward secrecy uses ephemeral key exchange so each session key is independent; compromising the long-term private key later does not allow decryption of past recorded sessions. Key escrow (A) stores copies of keys with a third party for recovery, which is the opposite concern. Salting (B) strengthens password hashes. Certificate pinning (C) ties an application to a specific certificate or public key to resist man-in-the-middle attacks, and does not affect session key derivation.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Ephemeral DH per session provides perfect forward secrecy. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A mobile banking app is hardcoded to only trust one specific certificate (or public key) for its API server, rejecting connections even if a different, otherwise valid certificate is presented by a server claiming to be the API endpoint. This technique is known as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Certificate pinning hardcodes the expected certificate or public key into the app, so any other certificate is rejected even if a CA signed it, mitigating man-in-the-middle attacks. Certificate chaining (B) is the hierarchy from root CA to end-entity certificate used in normal validation. Key escrow (C) stores keys with a third party for recovery. OCSP stapling (D) is a revocation-checking optimization and does not restrict which certificate is trusted.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Hardcoding trust to a specific certificate/public key is certificate pinning. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A web server is configured to periodically obtain a signed, time-stamped revocation status response from its CA's OCSP responder and include that response directly within the TLS handshake when a client connects, rather than requiring the client to separately contact the OCSP responder. This optimization is known as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. With OCSP stapling, the server periodically obtains a signed, time-stamped status response from the CA's OCSP responder and "staples" it to the TLS handshake, so clients do not have to contact the responder themselves. Key escrow (B) stores key copies for recovery. CRL distribution (C) is the older approach of publishing full revocation lists that clients download. Certificate pinning (D) restricts an application to one specific certificate and is unrelated to revocation checking.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Server caching and presenting the OCSP response in the handshake is OCSP stapling. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A government agency requires that a copy of every employee's encryption key be securely stored with a trusted internal authority so that encrypted data can still be recovered if an employee leaves the organization or loses their key. This practice is known as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Key escrow stores copies of encryption keys with a trusted authority so data can be recovered if the key holder leaves or loses the key. Key stretching (A) strengthens passwords or weak keys against brute force by adding computational work. Steganography (C) hides data inside other files. Perfect forward secrecy (D) makes past sessions unrecoverable after a future key compromise, which is the opposite of recoverability.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Storing copies of keys with a trusted authority for recovery is key escrow. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An analyst is comparing data-hiding techniques. Which TWO of the following statements correctly describe steganography and obfuscation? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Steganography hides the existence of data by embedding it within another file, such as concealing a text message within the pixel data of an image
Obfuscation makes data or code difficult to understand or read, such as renaming variables to meaningless characters, without necessarily hiding that something is present
Steganography and obfuscation both provide mathematically provable confidentiality equivalent to strong encryption
Obfuscation is a form of asymmetric encryption that uses a public and private key pair
Steganography always requires a CA-issued digital certificate to function

questions.justification:
Steganography conceals the existence of data by hiding it within another file or medium, such as embedding a message in an image's pixel data, so an observer may not even realize hidden data is present. Obfuscation makes data, code, or logic difficult to understand without necessarily hiding its existence, such as minifying or renaming variables in source code. Neither technique provides the mathematically provable confidentiality of strong encryption (C), since both can often be reversed by someone who knows the technique used. Obfuscation is not a form of asymmetric encryption (D) and does not use key pairs. Steganography does not require a digital certificate (E) to function.

CompTIA logic: Steganography and obfuscation are sometimes mistaken for encryption because all three relate to 'hiding' information, but neither provides the strong, key-based mathematical guarantees of encryption β€” they are best thought of as concealment or complexity techniques rather than true cryptographic protection.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Steganography hides existence of data; obfuscation makes it hard to understand.

questions.question: A payment processor replaces customers' actual credit card numbers stored in its database with randomly generated reference values that have no mathematical relationship to the original numbers. The mapping between the reference values and the real card numbers is kept in a separate, highly secured vault. Compared to encrypting the card numbers directly, this approach is BEST described as:

options.text: Tokenization, which removes the sensitive data from the database entirely by substituting it with a non-mathematically-derived reference value
Key stretching, because the token requires additional computational rounds to generate
Symmetric encryption, because both the token and the original value are derived using the same shared key
Hashing, because the token is a fixed-length irreversible representation of the card number

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Tokenization replaces the card numbers with random tokens that have no mathematical relationship to the originals; the mapping is kept in a separate secure vault, reducing PCI DSS scope. Key stretching (B) hardens passwords with extra hash iterations. Symmetric encryption (C) produces ciphertext mathematically derived from the plaintext and reversible with the key, which is not the case for random tokens. Hashing (D) is one-way, while tokens can be reversed through the vault lookup.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Random vault-mapped substitutes for card numbers are tokenization. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A security architect needs the fastest encryption approach for bulk data on a high-throughput database replication link. Which statement correctly distinguishes symmetric from asymmetric encryption for this use case?
tags: Cryptographic Solutions - Symmetric vs Asymmetric Review

options.text: Asymmetric encryption is faster than symmetric encryption for bulk data
Symmetric and asymmetric encryption perform at identical speeds
Symmetric encryption is faster than asymmetric encryption for bulk data encryption
Asymmetric encryption is preferred for bulk data because it uses a public/private key pair

questions.justification:
Symmetric encryption is significantly faster than asymmetric encryption for bulk data because it uses a single shared key and computationally simpler operations. This is why protocols like TLS use asymmetric encryption only to exchange the session key, then switch to symmetric (e.g., AES) for all data transmission. Asymmetric algorithms like RSA involve computationally expensive modular exponentiation, making them impractical for large-volume data encryption.

CompTIA logic: Hybrid encryption exists for exactly this reason: asymmetric for key exchange (solves distribution but is slow), symmetric for bulk data (fast but requires a pre-shared key). CompTIA tests this distinction frequently.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Symmetric encryption is faster for bulk data; options are simple statements.

questions.question: A developer is choosing a hashing algorithm to verify file integrity for a new application. Which of the following algorithms is currently considered cryptographically strong and suitable for this purpose?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. SHA-256, part of the SHA-2 family, is currently considered cryptographically strong and suitable for integrity verification. MD5 (A) and SHA-1 (B) have practical collision attacks and should not be used for security-relevant integrity checks. ROT13 (C) is a trivial letter-substitution scheme, neither a hash function nor secure in any way. For new applications, SHA-256 or stronger (SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-3) is the expected choice.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - SHA-256 is the only strong hash listed; MD5 and SHA-1 are broken. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An API gateway requires that every request include a value computed by combining the request body with a shared secret key using a cryptographic hash function. The receiving server recomputes this value using the same shared secret and compares it to the submitted value to confirm both the integrity of the request and that it was generated by a party who knows the shared secret. This mechanism is known as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. An HMAC combines a hash function with a shared secret key; only parties with the key can produce a matching value, so it proves both integrity and authenticity of the request. Salting (A) adds random data to passwords before hashing to defeat rainbow tables. Tokenization (B) replaces sensitive values with non-derivable tokens. OCSP (C) checks certificate revocation status and has nothing to do with message authentication codes.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Hash plus shared secret key for integrity and authenticity is HMAC. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A user wants to digitally sign a document so that recipients can verify both its integrity and its origin. Which of the following correctly describes the process?

options.text: The user encrypts the document using a shared symmetric key that both parties exchanged in advance over the phone

The user hashes the document, then encrypts the resulting hash with their own private key; recipients decrypt the signature using the user's public key and compare it to a hash they compute themselves
The user hashes the document and encrypts the hash with the recipient's public key, which only the recipient can decrypt with their private key
The user encrypts the entire document with the recipient's public key, and the recipient decrypts it with their own private key

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. A digital signature is created by hashing the document and encrypting the hash with the signer's private key; recipients decrypt it with the signer's public key and compare it with their own hash, proving integrity and origin. Option A uses a pre-shared symmetric key, which cannot prove which party created the message. Option C uses the recipient's public key, which provides confidentiality to the recipient, not proof of the sender. Option D encrypts the whole document for confidentiality and does not sign it.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Signing = hash then encrypt the hash with the signer private key; verify with the public key. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A browser receives a web server's certificate, which was signed by an intermediate CA, whose own certificate was signed by a root CA that is pre-installed in the browser's trust store. The browser is able to validate the web server's certificate by following this hierarchy back to a trusted root. This concept is known as the:
tags: Cryptographic Solutions - Certificate Chain of Trust
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. The chain of trust links the server certificate to an intermediate CA and then to a root CA in the browser's trust store, allowing validation by following signatures up the hierarchy. "Key escrow hierarchy" (A) is not a real concept; key escrow stores keys for recovery. Certificate pinning (B) restricts trust to one specific certificate regardless of the chain. A tokenization vault (C) maps tokens to sensitive data and has nothing to do with certificate validation.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Validating up to a trusted root through intermediates is the chain of trust. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A security architect is evaluating long-term risks to the organization's current RSA and ECC-based encryption deployments. Which emerging technology poses a theoretical future risk of being able to break these widely used asymmetric algorithms by efficiently solving the mathematical problems they rely on?
tags: Cryptographic Solutions - Emerging Threats to Cryptography
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer running Shor's algorithm could efficiently solve integer factorization and discrete logarithms, breaking RSA and ECC; this drives post-quantum cryptography. Federated identity management (A) is an authentication model, not a cryptanalytic threat. Containerization (B) is a virtualization technology. Software-defined networking (D) separates network control and data planes; neither affects the mathematical strength of asymmetric algorithms.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Quantum computing (Shor) threatens RSA and ECC. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A supply chain management system records each transaction in a sequential, cryptographically linked structure where each new entry includes a hash of the previous entry, making it computationally impractical to alter historical records without detection. This structure is BEST described as a:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. A blockchain or distributed ledger links each entry to the hash of the previous one, so altering any historical record changes its hash and breaks the chain, making tampering evident. A honeynet (A) is a decoy network for studying attackers. A key escrow vault (B) stores keys for recovery. A screened subnet (D) is a network zone for public-facing services; none of these creates an immutable transaction record.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Hash-linked sequential records are a blockchain/distributed ledger. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question:
During a TLS handshake between a client and a web server, the client sends a list of cipher suites it supports, and the server selects one cipher suite from that list to use for the session. The chosen cipher suite specifies the key exchange algorithm, the authentication algorithm, the bulk encryption algorithm, and the hashing algorithm used for the connection.

If the server selects a cipher suite that uses ephemeral Diffie-Hellman (DHE or ECDHE) for key exchange instead of static RSA key exchange, what security benefit is gained for this session?
tags: Cryptographic Solutions - TLS Handshake and Cipher Suites

options.text: Perfect forward secrecy, because a unique ephemeral key is generated for this session and is not derivable from the server's long-term private key
The session will use a weaker encryption algorithm than RSA key exchange would provide
The session will bypass the need for any symmetric encryption algorithm
The client no longer needs to validate the server's certificate

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman (DHE/ECDHE) creates a unique key per session that cannot be derived from the server's long-term private key, giving perfect forward secrecy. Option B is wrong because the key exchange choice does not weaken the separately negotiated bulk cipher. Option C is wrong because TLS always uses a symmetric cipher for bulk data after the handshake. Option D is wrong because the client still validates the server certificate regardless of the key exchange method.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - DHE/ECDHE key exchange provides perfect forward secrecy. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An application stores user passwords as hashed values. To protect against precomputed hash attacks and brute-force attacks, the developers add random data to each password before hashing and also run the hash function through thousands of iterations. Which TWO of the following correctly describe these two techniques? (Choose TWO.)
tags: Cryptographic Solutions - Salting vs Key Stretching

options.text: Salting adds unique random data to each password before hashing, which prevents attackers from using precomputed rainbow tables across multiple accounts
Key stretching applies the hash function repeatedly (many iterations), which increases the computational cost of each brute-force guess
Salting and key stretching both eliminate the need to ever store a hashed password
Salting encrypts the password using the recipient's public key before hashing
Key stretching is only applicable to symmetric encryption keys, never to passwords

questions.justification: Salting adds unique random data to each password before hashing so that identical passwords produce different hash values and precomputed rainbow tables become ineffective. Key stretching applies the hash function through many iterations (or uses algorithms designed for this purpose, such as PBKDF2, bcrypt, or Argon2), making each brute-force attempt computationally expensive. Both techniques still result in a stored hash (C is incorrect). Salting does not involve public key encryption (D). Key stretching is commonly applied to passwords specifically to slow down brute-force attacks, not only to symmetric keys (E).
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Salting defeats rainbow tables and key stretching raises brute-force cost.

questions.question: A company hosts several subdomains (mail.example.com, vpn.example.com, and portal.example.com) on different servers and wants to use a single certificate that secures all of them, including any future subdomains, without reissuing the certificate each time a new subdomain is added. Which type of certificate BEST meets this requirement?
tags: Cryptographic Solutions - Wildcard and SAN Certificates

options.text: A self-signed certificate generated independently on each server

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. A wildcard certificate for *.example.com covers any first-level subdomain, including ones added later, without reissuing. An OCSP responder certificate (A) signs revocation responses and does not secure websites. A CRL (C) is a list of revoked certificates, not a certificate. Self-signed certificates on each server (D) are not trusted by browsers and would have to be managed per server. A SAN certificate is an alternative, but it must be reissued to add new names.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A wildcard certificate covers current and future first-level subdomains. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A developer installs a self-signed TLS certificate on a company's public-facing customer portal. What issue will most customers experience when visiting the site?

options.text: The site will function identically to one with a CA-issued certificate with no user-visible impact
The browser will display a trust warning because the certificate was not issued by a trusted CA
The site will be completely inaccessible since browsers fully block self-signed certificates
Self-signed certificates are stronger than CA-issued certificates because they are generated locally

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Browsers only trust certificates chaining to a CA in their trust store, so a self-signed certificate triggers a warning because the server identity cannot be verified. Option A is wrong because the warning is visible to users. Option C is wrong because browsers usually let users click through rather than blocking access completely. Option D is wrong because self-signed certificates are not cryptographically stronger; they simply lack third-party identity verification.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Self-signed certificates trigger browser trust warnings. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A cloud storage provider encrypts each customer's file using a unique data encryption key (DEK). That DEK is then itself encrypted using a separate, centrally managed key encryption key (KEK), and only the encrypted DEK is stored alongside the file. This layered approach is known as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Envelope encryption encrypts data with a data encryption key and then encrypts that DEK with a centrally managed key encryption key, often held in a KMS or HSM, simplifying rotation and control. Steganography (A) hides data inside other files. Certificate pinning (B) restricts trust to a specific certificate. Key stretching (D) strengthens weak keys or passwords with extra computation and is not a layered key hierarchy.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - DEK encrypted by a KEK is envelope encryption. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question:
A developer on the e-commerce platform team runs a routine audit of the company's GitHub repositories using a secrets-scanning tool (truffleHog) and discovers that a colleague accidentally committed the RSA private key for the production web server's TLS certificate to a public GitHub repository at 2:47 AM during an emergency hotfix push. The repository was public for approximately 4 hours before the commit was force-removed and the repo made private. The TLS certificate, issued by DigiCert, is currently valid and not set to expire for another 11 months. The CISO asks the security team to determine the correct immediate response under the assumption that the private key must be treated as fully compromised.

What is the MOST appropriate immediate action for the security team to take?
tags: Cryptographic Solutions - Private Key Compromise Response

options.text: Increase the certificate's validity period to reduce how often this could happen again
Wait until the certificate's normal expiration date in 11 months, since revocation is unnecessary if the key was only exposed briefly
Change the website's domain name to prevent the compromised key from being used
Revoke the compromised certificate with the issuing CA and request a new certificate using a newly generated key pair

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D.
