Microservices (A) describes decomposing applications into services. Serverless (B) describes how compute is provisioned and billed. Decentralized (C) describes the second option, with no single central authority.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A single central directory for credentials and decisions is a centralized architecture. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A security analyst reviewing firewall logs wants to identify all traffic using the standard encrypted web protocol. Which destination port is associated with HTTPS?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. HTTPS uses TCP port 443 for TLS-encrypted web traffic by default. Port 8443 (A) is a common alternate HTTPS port for management interfaces, but not the standard. Port 8080 (C) is an alternate HTTP port often used by proxies and development servers. Port 80 (D) is unencrypted HTTP. Filtering on 443 therefore captures standard encrypted web traffic, while traffic on alternate ports needs separate rules.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - HTTPS uses TCP 443. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A network administrator troubleshooting DNS resolution failures needs to verify that the firewall allows DNS query traffic to the internal resolver. Which port number must be open for DNS queries?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. DNS uses port 53, UDP for most queries and TCP for zone transfers and large responses, so it must be open to the internal resolver. Port 25 (B) is SMTP mail relay. Port 143 (C) is unencrypted IMAP email retrieval. Port 389 (D) is LDAP directory access. None of these carry DNS queries. Key takeaway: the details in this scenario point to 53.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - DNS uses port 53. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An email security administrator is configuring a firewall to allow server-to-server email relay between Mail Transfer Agents (MTAs) while blocking direct client-to-server mail submission on the same port. Which port is traditionally used for MTA-to-MTA email relay via SMTP?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Port 25 is the traditional SMTP port for server-to-server (MTA-to-MTA) relay. Port 465 (A) is SMTPS with implicit TLS, typically for client submission. Port 110 (B) is POP3 for retrieving mail. Port 587 (D) is the message submission port clients use to send authenticated outgoing mail, which the scenario wants handled separately from relay. Key takeaway: the details in this scenario point to 25.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - MTA-to-MTA relay uses SMTP port 25. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A security team is auditing firewall rules and finds port 110 allowed inbound to an email server. Which unencrypted email retrieval protocol uses this port?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. POP3 uses TCP port 110 for unencrypted email retrieval (POP3S uses 995). SMTP (A) sends mail rather than retrieving it. IMAP (C) also retrieves mail but uses port 143 unencrypted or 993 with TLS. SMTPS (D) is encrypted SMTP on port 465, again used for sending mail. Finding 110 open suggests credentials may travel in cleartext, so POP3S or IMAPS should be preferred.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - POP3 uses TCP 110. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A security engineer needs to block unencrypted email inbox access while allowing encrypted IMAPS (port 993). Which port should be blocked to stop unencrypted IMAP connections?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Unencrypted IMAP uses TCP port 143; blocking it while allowing 993 (IMAPS) enforces encrypted mailbox access. Port 445 (A) is SMB file sharing. Port 110 (B) is unencrypted POP3, a different retrieval protocol. Port 389 (D) is LDAP directory access. Blocking 110 as well would be needed to stop unencrypted POP3, but the question asks specifically about IMAP, whose cleartext port is 143.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Unencrypted IMAP uses TCP 143. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: Before a laptop is permitted to communicate on a corporate wired or wireless network, it must first authenticate through a port-based access control protocol, with an authentication server validating the device's credentials before the switch or access point opens the port for general traffic. Which standard BEST describes this port-based network access control mechanism?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. IEEE 802.1X is port-based network access control: the switch or access point keeps the port closed until an authentication server, typically RADIUS, validates the device or user. RDP (A) is a remote desktop protocol. WPA2 (B) is a Wi-Fi security protocol; its Enterprise mode uses 802.1X, but it is not itself the port-based framework. 802.11 (C) is the family of wireless LAN standards and defines Wi-Fi communication, not admission control.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Port-based network access control requiring authentication before the port opens is 802.1X. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A network engineer is selecting an Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) variant for an 802.1X wireless deployment. Which TWO of the following statements about EAP variants are accurate? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: EAP-TLS requires both the client and the server to have digital certificates, providing mutual certificate-based authentication
PEAP (Protected EAP) creates an encrypted TLS tunnel using a server-side certificate, within which a client can authenticate using a method such as a username and password
EAP-TTLS requires every client device to have its own certificate before any tunnel can be established
EAP variants are interchangeable with WPA2-Personal and provide identical functionality
PEAP and EAP-TLS both completely eliminate the need for any server-side certificate

questions.justification:
EAP-TLS provides mutual authentication using digital certificates on both the client and server, offering strong security but requiring certificate management for every client. PEAP establishes an encrypted TLS tunnel using only a server-side certificate, and within that protected tunnel, the client can authenticate using a simpler method such as a username and password, reducing client-side certificate management overhead. EAP-TTLS, like PEAP, only requires a server-side certificate to establish the tunnel, not a certificate on every client (C is incorrect). EAP variants are specifically used with 802.1X/WPA2-Enterprise (or WPA3-Enterprise), not WPA2-Personal, which uses a pre-shared key instead (D is incorrect). Both PEAP and EAP-TTLS require a server-side certificate to establish their protective tunnel, and EAP-TLS requires certificates on both ends, so server-side certificates are not eliminated (E is incorrect).

CompTIA logic: EAP-TLS, PEAP, and EAP-TTLS differ primarily in certificate requirements: EAP-TLS requires certificates on BOTH client and server (strongest but highest administrative overhead); PEAP and EAP-TTLS require a certificate only on the SERVER, using that certificate to build an encrypted tunnel within which the client authenticates via a simpler method like a password, trading some security rigor for easier deployment.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - EAP-TLS needs certificates on both sides; PEAP uses a server certificate and inner password authentication.

questions.question: A company's inline intrusion prevention system (IPS) experiences a hardware failure. Network traffic continues to pass through the device uninspected rather than being blocked entirely, ensuring business operations are not interrupted, but leaving the network temporarily without IPS inspection. This failure behavior is known as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Fail-open means that when the security device fails, traffic keeps flowing uninspected, favoring availability over security. Load balancing (B) spreads traffic across devices for performance. Active-active clustering (C) has several devices handling traffic simultaneously for redundancy. Fail-closed (D) is the opposite behavior: all traffic is blocked when the device fails, favoring security over availability. Key takeaway: the details in this scenario point to Fail-open.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Traffic passing uninspected when the device fails is fail-open. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A network security team deploys a sensor that connects to a switch's mirrored port, receiving a copy of all network traffic for analysis, without being positioned directly in the path that live traffic travels through. This deployment method is known as:
tags: Network Appliances - Inline vs Tap/Monitor Mode
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. A sensor receiving a copy of traffic from a mirrored (SPAN) port or network tap is deployed in passive tap/monitor mode; it can analyze but not block traffic in real time. Full tunnel (A) is a VPN routing mode. Inline mode (B) places the device directly in the traffic path so it can block, which is the opposite. Fail-closed (D) describes behavior on failure, not deployment topology.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A sensor on a mirrored/SPAN port is passive tap/monitor mode. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization wants to control and log which websites its employees can access from their workstations, cache frequently accessed content to improve performance, and potentially hide the internal IP addresses of workstations from external websites. Which device BEST provides these capabilities?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. A forward proxy sits between internal clients and the internet, so it can filter and log the sites employees visit, cache content and hide internal client IP addresses. A load balancer (A) distributes inbound requests across servers. A reverse proxy (B) sits in front of internal servers handling inbound requests from external clients, the opposite direction. A jump server (D) is a hardened host for administrative access.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Filtering, logging and caching outbound web requests is a forward proxy. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A load balancer distributes incoming web requests across a pool of three web servers by sending each new request to the next server in the pool in sequential order, cycling back to the first server after reaching the last. This load balancing method is known as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Round-robin sends each new request to the next server in sequence and cycles back to the first, spreading load evenly across servers of similar capacity. Full tunnel (B) is a VPN mode. Geographic dispersion (C) spreads systems across locations for resilience. Active-passive failover (D) keeps a standby system idle until the primary fails instead of distributing live traffic among servers.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Sequential cyclic distribution of requests is round-robin. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A database administrator is hardening firewall rules and needs to block external internet access to the organization's Microsoft SQL Server instances to prevent direct database attacks. Which destination port should be blocked from internet-facing traffic?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Microsoft SQL Server listens on TCP port 1433 by default, so that port should be blocked from internet-facing traffic. Port 3306 (A) is MySQL/MariaDB. Port 5432 (B) is PostgreSQL. Port 1521 (D) is the Oracle Database listener. Database ports should never be directly exposed to the internet; access should go through application tiers or VPNs. Key takeaway: the details in this scenario point to 1433.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Microsoft SQL Server listens on TCP 1433. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: During a penetration test, an assessor scans a web server and finds TCP port 3306 open and accessible from the internet. This is flagged as a critical finding. Which database service is directly exposed by this open port?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. TCP port 3306 is the default for MySQL and MariaDB, so an internet-exposed 3306 means the MySQL service is reachable for brute force or exploitation. Oracle Database (A) uses 1521. Microsoft SQL Server Express (B) and Microsoft SQL Server (D) use 1433 by default (Express often uses dynamic ports with the Browser service on UDP 1434). Key takeaway: the details in this scenario point to MySQL.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - TCP 3306 is MySQL. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A VoIP security engineer is configuring a session border controller and needs to identify the port associated with the SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) for VoIP call signaling in order to apply the correct firewall rules. Which port number is used for SIP?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. SIP uses port 5060 over UDP or TCP for VoIP call signaling (5061 for SIP over TLS). Port 8080 (A) is an alternate HTTP port used by proxies and web applications. Port 5900 (C) is VNC remote desktop. Port 3389 (D) is Microsoft RDP. Only 5060 matches SIP signaling for the session border controller rules. Key takeaway: the details in this scenario point to 5060.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - SIP signaling uses port 5060. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A small business wants a single appliance that combines firewall, antivirus, content filtering, VPN, and intrusion prevention functions into one consolidated, easy-to-manage product, prioritizing simplicity over highly granular, application-specific controls. Which type of appliance is generally MOST associated with this all-in-one, simplicity-focused approach?

options.text: Next-generation firewall (NGFW) focused on deep application-layer policy granularity
A standalone Layer 4 packet-filtering firewall only

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. A unified threat management appliance bundles firewall, antivirus, content filtering, VPN and IPS in one easy-to-manage product, which suits a small business. An NGFW focused on deep application-layer granularity (A) targets complex environments needing fine-grained policy. A standalone Layer 4 packet filter (C) provides only IP/port filtering. A jump server (D) is an administrative access host and not a security appliance of this kind.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - An all-in-one, simplicity-focused appliance is a UTM. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question:
A manufacturing company has a single flat network where office workstations, guest Wi-Fi devices, and factory floor industrial control systems all share the same broadcast domain and IP subnet. After a guest device becomes infected with malware, the malware is able to scan and attempt connections to the industrial control systems directly.

Which network design change would BEST prevent this type of incident from recurring?

options.text: Implement VLANs to segment guest devices, office workstations, and industrial control systems into separate logical networks with firewall rules controlling traffic between them
Increase the IP address range of the single flat network to accommodate more devices
Disable DHCP so that devices must use static IP addresses on the same shared subnet
Enable full tunnel VPN for all guest Wi-Fi users

questions.justification:
Implementing VLANs creates separate logical broadcast domains for different device groups, such as guest devices, office workstations, and industrial control systems, and combining this with firewall rules between VLANs ensures that a compromised device in one segment cannot directly reach systems in another segment, directly addressing the root cause of this incident. Simply increasing the IP address range (B) does not create any segmentation or access control between device types. Disabling DHCP (C) does not prevent devices on the same flat subnet from communicating with each other; it only changes how addresses are assigned. Enabling a full tunnel VPN for guest users (D) addresses how guest traffic is routed to the internet but does not segment guest devices from internal industrial systems on the local network.

CompTIA logic: Network segmentation (via VLANs and firewall rules between them) is the standard remediation for incidents where a compromise in one device class spreads laterally to a more sensitive device class on the same flat network, because it directly limits the blast radius of any single compromised device.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - VLAN segmentation with inter-VLAN firewall rules isolates guests from ICS.

questions.question: A company wants to prevent employees from accessing social media and streaming video sites during work hours using a security tool that can inspect web traffic and categorize URLs in real time. Which security tool BEST accomplishes this?
tags: Network Appliances - Secure Web Gateway / Content Filtering

options.text: Secure Web Gateway (SWG) with URL content categorization

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. A secure web gateway with URL categorization inspects outbound web traffic and blocks categories such as social media and streaming according to policy. A stateful packet inspection firewall alone (A) filters by IP, port and connection state without URL categories. An IDS (C) detects intrusions and alerts but does not enforce web content policy. A SIEM (D) aggregates and correlates logs and does not block traffic.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - URL categorization and web content filtering is done by a secure web gateway. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization labels its documents using categories such as 'Public,' 'Internal Use Only,' 'Confidential,' and 'Restricted,' with handling requirements becoming stricter for each higher level. This labeling system is an example of:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Assigning sensitivity labels such as Public, Internal Use Only, Confidential and Restricted, each with stricter handling rules, is data classification. Geographic dispersion (A) spreads systems across locations for resilience. Data masking (B) obscures parts of data values for display or testing. Tokenization (D) replaces sensitive values with tokens; none of these are labeling schemes. Key takeaway: the details in this scenario point to Data classification.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Public/Internal/Confidential/Restricted labels are data classification. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A hospital's database contains patients' names, addresses, Social Security numbers, and also their diagnoses, treatment histories, and prescribed medications. Which term specifically refers to the diagnosis, treatment, and medication information, as distinct from the names and Social Security numbers?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Diagnoses, treatment histories and medications linked to an identifiable patient are Protected Health Information, regulated by HIPAA. Data sovereignty (B) is the principle that data is subject to the laws where it is stored. Infrastructure as code (C) is an architecture concept. PII (D) covers identifiers such as names and SSNs, but the question asks for the term specific to health data, which is PHI.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Health information linked to an individual is PHI. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A company headquartered in the United States stores its European customers' data on servers located in Germany. A German regulator asserts that this data is subject to German and European Union data protection laws because of where it is physically stored and processed, regardless of where the company is headquartered. This concept, that data is subject to the laws of the country in which it is located, is known as:
questions.justification: Data sovereignty refers to the principle that data is subject to the laws and regulations of the country in which it is physically stored or processed, which has significant implications for multinational organizations deciding where to host data. Data masking (B) involves obscuring data values for display, unrelated to jurisdictional law. Tokenization (C) is a data protection technique substituting tokens for sensitive values. The right to be forgotten (D) is a specific GDPR provision allowing individuals to request deletion of their personal data, which is related to but distinct from the broader concept of which country's laws apply based on data location.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Data being subject to the laws of the country where it resides is data sovereignty.

questions.question: Under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), several distinct roles are defined regarding personal data. Which TWO of the following statements correctly describe these roles? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: The data controller determines the purposes and means of processing personal data
The data processor processes personal data on behalf of, and under the instructions of, the data controller
The data subject is the organization that decides why and how personal data will be processed
A data processor automatically becomes the data controller as soon as it stores any data
GDPR roles only apply to companies physically located within the European Union

questions.justification:
Under GDPR, the data controller is the entity that determines the purposes and means of processing personal data, while the data processor processes that data on behalf of, and under the instructions of, the controller, such as a cloud service provider processing data for a client company. The data subject (C) is actually the individual to whom the personal data relates, not an organization, so this statement incorrectly defines that role. A data processor does not automatically become a controller simply by storing data (D is incorrect); its role is defined by its relationship and instructions, not merely by possession. GDPR can apply to organizations outside the EU if they process the personal data of EU residents, so it is not limited to companies physically located within the EU (E is incorrect).

CompTIA logic: Data controller, data processor, and data subject are frequently tested GDPR roles. The controller decides 'why and how' (purpose and means), the processor acts on the controller's instructions ('how, but not why'), and the data subject is the individual the data is ABOUT, not an organization handling the data at all.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Controller determines purposes/means; processor acts on the controller behalf.

questions.question: An EU citizen contacts a company subject to GDPR requesting that all personal data collected about them — including purchase history and marketing preferences — be permanently deleted from the company's systems. Which right under GDPR is the citizen exercising?
tags: Data Protection - Right to Be Forgotten

options.text: Right to be forgotten (right to erasure)

questions.justification: The right to be forgotten (also called the right to erasure) under GDPR Article 17 allows individuals to request permanent deletion of their personal data under certain conditions, such as when the data is no longer necessary for its original purpose or consent has been withdrawn. The right to access (A) allows individuals to obtain a copy of their data. The right to data portability (B) allows data to be transferred to another controller. The right to restrict processing (D) limits how data is used without requiring deletion.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Requesting deletion of personal data is the right to be forgotten (erasure).

questions.question: An organization establishes a policy specifying that customer transaction records must be kept for seven years to meet regulatory requirements, after which they must be securely destroyed. This policy is an example of:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. A data retention policy defines how long data must be kept to meet legal, regulatory or business requirements and how it is securely destroyed afterward. Data masking (B) obscures data values for display. An incident response plan (C) defines how to handle security incidents. Tokenization (D) replaces sensitive values with tokens. None of these define storage duration and disposal.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Keeping records seven years then destroying them is a data retention policy. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: During the design of a new customer registration form, a privacy officer insists that the form should only collect the specific data fields that are strictly necessary for the intended business purpose, rather than collecting every field that might possibly be useful in the future. This principle is BEST described as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Data minimization means collecting and retaining only the data strictly needed for a defined purpose, which reduces exposure if a breach occurs. Geographic dispersion (B) spreads systems across locations for resilience. Data sovereignty (C) concerns which country's laws apply based on where data resides. Tokenization (D) protects data already collected rather than limiting what is collected. Key takeaway: the details in this scenario point to Data minimization.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Collecting only strictly necessary fields is data minimization. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A compliance officer classifying data stored in the HR system identifies which of the following sets as PII (Personally Identifiable Information) that must be protected under applicable regulations?

options.text: Software version numbers and application license keys
An employee's full name, Social Security number, and home address
Aggregated, anonymized salary band statistics with no individual identifiers
Server IP addresses and operating system version numbers

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. A full name combined with a Social Security number and home address identifies a specific person, so it is PII that must be protected. Software versions and license keys (A) are asset inventory data. Aggregated, anonymized salary statistics (C) contain no individual identifiers. Server IP addresses and OS versions (D) are technical configuration data, not information about a person.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Name, SSN and home address together are PII. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A healthcare organization is assessing which data in its systems falls under HIPAA protections. Which of the following would be classified as PHI (Protected Health Information)?

options.text: A patient's name, diagnosis, and date of treatment linked together in a medical record
Publicly available information about hospital visiting hours
An anonymized statistical study of regional flu rates with no individual identifiers
Generic medical device operational log files containing no patient data

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. PHI is individually identifiable health information: a patient's name linked with a diagnosis and date of treatment in a medical record. Public visiting-hours information (B) is not about any individual. An anonymized flu-rate study (C) contains no identifiers. Device operational logs without patient data (D) contain no health information about a person, so none of these are PHI under HIPAA.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Name plus diagnosis and treatment date linked in a record is PHI. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question:
A SaaS company based in the United States serves customers in the European Union and stores all customer data, including EU residents' personal data, exclusively on servers located in the United States. EU regulators raise concerns about whether this arrangement complies with EU data protection requirements regarding personal data of EU residents.

This scenario PRIMARILY illustrates which data protection concept, and what is a common approach companies use to address it?

options.text: Data sovereignty and cross-border data transfer concerns; companies often address this by storing EU residents' data in EU-based data centers or using approved legal transfer mechanisms
Data masking concerns; the company should mask all customer names before storing any data
Right to be forgotten concerns; the company should automatically delete all data after 24 hours
Tokenization concerns; the company should tokenize all server hostnames

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Storing EU residents' personal data only in the US raises data sovereignty and cross-border transfer concerns; companies respond with EU data residency or approved legal transfer mechanisms. Masking customer names (B) does not change where data is stored or which laws apply. Deleting all data after 24 hours (C) misapplies the right to be forgotten and would break the service. Tokenizing server hostnames (D) is irrelevant to jurisdiction.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - EU personal data stored in the US raises data sovereignty/cross-border transfer concerns. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: Within an organization's data governance program, one role is accountable for the overall use and protection of a specific dataset and makes decisions about its classification, while a separate role is responsible for the day-to-day technical management of the systems storing that data, such as performing backups and applying access controls. Which two roles are being described, respectively?
tags: Data Protection - Data Roles (Owner, Steward, Custodian)

options.text: Data steward and data sovereignty officer

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. The data owner is accountable for a dataset and decides its classification, while the data custodian (usually IT) performs day-to-day technical management such as backups and access control implementation. Processor and controller (A) are GDPR roles between organizations. Subject and controller (B) are the individual the data is about and the entity deciding processing. "Data sovereignty officer" (C) is not a standard governance role.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Accountable business role is data owner; day-to-day technical manager is data custodian. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization is documenting the stages that data passes through from the moment it is collected until it is permanently destroyed. Which TWO of the following are commonly recognized stages in the data lifecycle? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Data creation/collection, where data first enters the organization's systems
Data destruction/disposal, where data is securely and permanently removed at the end of its useful life
Data sovereignty, which is a stage that always occurs immediately before data creation
Tokenization, which is the final and only stage of every data lifecycle
Data lifecycles apply only to data stored in cloud environments, never to on-premises data

questions.justification: The data lifecycle typically includes stages such as creation/collection, storage, use, sharing, archiving, and ultimately destruction/disposal, governing how data is handled appropriately at each stage. Data sovereignty (C) is a legal/jurisdictional concept, not a lifecycle stage that precedes creation. Tokenization (D) is a data protection technique that may be applied during the use or storage stages, not the sole final stage of every lifecycle. The data lifecycle concept applies to data regardless of whether it is stored on-premises or in the cloud (E is incorrect).
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Creation/collection and destruction are lifecycle stages; distractors are absurd.

questions.question: A research team processes a dataset of patient records by replacing each patient's name with a unique code, while maintaining a separate, securely stored key that maps each code back to the original patient name for authorized re-identification if needed. Which term BEST describes this technique?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Pseudonymization replaces identifiers with artificial codes but keeps a separate, secured mapping that allows authorized re-identification. Data sovereignty (A) concerns which laws apply based on data location. Data minimization (C) limits how much data is collected. Anonymization (D) irreversibly removes identifying information so no one can re-identify individuals, which is not the case when a key is retained.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Replacing names with codes while keeping a re-identification key is pseudonymization. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization subject to EU data protection regulations must ensure customer data from EU residents is never stored or processed on servers outside the European Economic Area. Which data protection mechanism BEST helps enforce this requirement?

options.text: Data masking of all EU customer fields
Tokenization of all EU customer records
Full disk encryption on all servers
Geographic restrictions and data residency controls

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Geographic restrictions and data residency controls ensure data is stored and processed only in approved regions, directly enforcing the EEA requirement. Data masking (A) and tokenization (B) protect data values but do not control where records reside. Full disk encryption (C) protects confidentiality at rest but data could still be stored on servers outside the EEA. Key takeaway: the details in this scenario point to Geographic restrictions and data residency controls.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Keeping EU data inside the EEA is enforced with geographic restrictions/data residency controls. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A data center wants to ensure that during a complete utility power outage, critical servers experience zero interruption, with backup power immediately and seamlessly taking over for a short period while a separate, larger power source spins up to handle a prolonged outage. Which device provides the immediate, seamless short-term power during this transition?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. An uninterruptible power supply provides instant battery power with zero interruption, bridging the gap until a generator starts and stabilizes. A diesel generator alone (A) needs time to start, so servers would lose power briefly. A load balancer (B) distributes network traffic and does nothing for power. A RAID array (D) provides disk redundancy, not power continuity.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A UPS provides immediate short-term power until the generator takes over. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A storage administrator configures an array of disks so that data is striped across multiple drives along with parity information, allowing the array to continue operating and reconstruct data even if a single drive fails, while using less total storage overhead than simply mirroring every drive. Which RAID level BEST matches this description?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. RAID 5 stripes data with distributed parity across three or more disks, survives a single disk failure and uses only one disk's worth of capacity for parity, less overhead than mirroring. RAID 0 (A) stripes without redundancy, so any disk failure loses data. A single disk (C) offers no fault tolerance. RAID 1 (D) mirrors disks, providing redundancy but with 100 percent storage overhead.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Striping with distributed parity tolerating one drive failure is RAID 5. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A company wants to design its data center to avoid single points of failure related to both power and network connectivity. Which TWO of the following design choices directly support this goal? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Provisioning power feeds from two separate utility substations
Connecting to two different internet service providers via diverse network paths
Storing all backup tapes in the same room as the production servers for convenience
Using only a single network switch to reduce configuration complexity
Relying on a single administrator who is familiar with all systems

questions.justification: Provisioning power from two separate substations ensures that a failure affecting one power source does not take down the entire facility, and connecting to two different ISPs via diverse paths ensures that a failure of one internet connection does not result in a total loss of connectivity, both directly addressing single points of failure. Storing backup tapes in the same room as production servers (C) actually creates a single point of failure, since a single disaster (such as a fire) could destroy both production data and backups. Using only a single network switch (D) creates a single point of failure for network connectivity. Relying on a single administrator (E) creates a single point of failure for operational knowledge and response capability.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Dual substation feeds and dual ISPs remove single points of failure.

questions.question: A company operates two data centers located in different regions of the country, several hundred miles apart, so that a regional natural disaster, such as a hurricane or earthquake, affecting one location is unlikely to impact the other. This design strategy is BEST described as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Placing data centers in different regions far enough apart that one regional disaster cannot affect both is geographic dispersion. RAID 1 mirroring (A) duplicates disks within one system. Tokenization (B) is a data protection technique unrelated to site placement. NIC teaming (D) provides network interface redundancy inside a single server. Only geographic separation protects against hurricanes, earthquakes or regional power failures.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Data centers hundreds of miles apart provide geographic dispersion. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A disaster recovery audit reveals an organization has been creating daily backups for three years but has never performed a test restoration. What risk does this MOST directly present?

options.text: The backups may be too large, consuming excessive storage capacity
Untested backups automatically expire after 90 days by industry standard
The backup software license may have expired, preventing future backups
The backups may be corrupted or incomplete, rendering them unusable when actually needed for recovery

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Backups that have never been test-restored may be corrupted, incomplete or unrestorable, and this is only discovered during a real disaster. Storage size (A) is a capacity concern, not a recovery risk. A lapsed backup software license (C) is speculative and unrelated to the lack of testing. There is no industry standard that makes untested backups expire after 90 days (B).
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Never-tested backups may be corrupted or unrestorable. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A company replicates its database to a secondary data center. In one configuration, every write to the primary database must be confirmed as written to the secondary site before the primary database acknowledges the write as complete, ensuring zero data loss but adding latency to every transaction. This replication method is known as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Synchronous replication acknowledges a write only after both primary and secondary have stored it, giving zero data loss (RPO of zero) at the cost of added latency. Incremental backup (A) periodically copies changed data. Asynchronous replication (C) acknowledges immediately and updates the secondary later, so some data can be lost. A snapshot (D) captures a point-in-time image, not continuous replication.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Acknowledging writes only after the secondary confirms is synchronous replication. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A storm causes significant damage to a company's headquarters. The organization activates its overarching plan that addresses how critical business operations will continue across all departments — including payroll, customer service, and logistics — during and after the disruption. This plan is called a:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. The Business Continuity Plan is the overarching plan for keeping critical business functions, such as payroll, customer service and logistics, running during and after a disruption. An SLA (A) is a contractual service performance commitment. An IRP (C) governs response to security incidents. A DRP (D) is the IT-focused subset of the BCP for restoring systems and data.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - An organization-wide plan to keep business functions running is the BCP. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: After a ransomware attack encrypts the majority of a company's servers, the IT team activates a specific plan focused on restoring IT systems, recovering data from backups, and bringing critical applications back online in priority order. This IT-focused recovery plan is called a:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. The Disaster Recovery Plan focuses on restoring IT systems and data from backups and bringing critical applications back in priority order. An IRP (A) covers detection, containment and investigation of the incident itself. An MOA (C) is an agreement between parties. A BCP (D) is the broader business-wide continuity plan that contains the DRP. Key takeaway: the details in this scenario point to DRP (Disaster Recovery Plan).
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - An IT-focused plan to restore systems and data is the DRP. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: Before launching a new service, an organization analyzes projected user growth over the next three years and provisions servers, storage, and network bandwidth to accommodate that anticipated future demand, rather than only meeting current needs. This process is known as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Capacity planning forecasts future compute, storage and bandwidth needs from expected growth and provisions resources ahead of demand to avoid performance problems or outages. Data masking (A) and tokenization (B) are data protection techniques. A tabletop exercise (D) is a discussion-based test of response or continuity plans. None of these forecast infrastructure needs. Key takeaway: the details in this scenario point to Capacity planning.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Forecasting and provisioning for future demand is capacity planning. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization deploys firewalls from two different vendors at different points in its network, reasoning that if a zero-day vulnerability is discovered in one vendor's product, the other vendor's devices, using different underlying code, are unlikely to share the exact same flaw. This strategy is an example of:

options.text: Vendor diversity as a resilience strategy

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Using firewalls from two vendors so a single zero-day is unlikely to affect both is vendor diversity, a resilience strategy that avoids common-mode failures. Data sovereignty (A) concerns laws that apply based on data location. Full tunnel VPN (B) routes all client traffic through the corporate network. Tokenization (D) replaces sensitive data with tokens; none relate to vendor selection.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Using firewalls from different vendors so one flaw does not affect all is vendor diversity. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question:
A company's disaster recovery plan calls for a full failover test once per year, in which production traffic is actually redirected to the secondary data center for a defined period to confirm that systems function correctly under real conditions, rather than only reviewing the plan on paper. During this year's test, the failover is initiated, but several applications fail to start correctly at the secondary site due to configuration drift that had occurred since the last test.

What is the PRIMARY value of conducting this type of full failover test, as illustrated by this scenario?
tags: Resilience - Continuity of Operations / Failover Test (PBQ)

options.text: It guarantees that no future failover will ever encounter any issues
It eliminates the need for any other type of disaster recovery testing in the future
It is purely a compliance checkbox exercise with no operational value
It identifies real-world gaps, such as configuration drift, that would not be discovered through a documentation review alone, allowing the organization to fix issues before an actual disaster occurs

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Actually failing over reveals real-world problems such as configuration drift that a document review would never uncover, so they can be fixed before a real disaster. No test can guarantee future failovers will be issue-free (A). A single full test does not replace other testing such as tabletops or partial tests (B). The scenario clearly shows operational value beyond a compliance checkbox (C).
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A full failover test reveals real-world gaps such as configuration drift. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A database server maintains a continuous log of every transaction as it occurs, separate from the main data files, so that if the database crashes, it can be restored to a consistent state by replaying or rolling back transactions recorded in this log since the last checkpoint. This logging mechanism is known as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Journaling records every transaction in a separate log so a database or file system can replay or roll back changes after a crash and return to a consistent state. Tokenization (A) substitutes sensitive values with tokens. Geographic dispersion (C) spreads systems across locations. Load balancing (D) distributes traffic across servers; none of these provide transaction-level crash recovery.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A transaction log replayed or rolled back after a crash is journaling. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A security team is planning exercises to validate its incident response and disaster recovery plans. Which TWO of the following statements correctly describe different types of testing exercises? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: A tabletop exercise is a discussion-based session where participants walk through their roles and responsibilities for a hypothetical scenario without actually performing technical recovery actions
A parallel processing test involves running recovery systems alongside production systems to validate that they function correctly, without taking production systems offline
Tabletop exercises require taking production systems completely offline for the duration of the exercise
A parallel processing test is identical to a tabletop exercise in terms of resource commitment and risk
Testing exercises serve no purpose once a written disaster recovery plan has been created

questions.justification:
A tabletop exercise is a low-risk, discussion-based walkthrough where participants talk through their responses to a hypothetical scenario without performing actual technical actions or affecting production systems, while a parallel processing test runs recovery systems alongside (in parallel with) production systems to validate functionality without disrupting normal operations, providing more realistic validation than a tabletop without the full risk of a complete failover. Tabletop exercises specifically do NOT require taking production offline (C is incorrect) β€” that is closer to a full interruption test. Parallel processing tests involve significantly more resource commitment and technical execution than tabletop exercises, so they are not identical (D is incorrect). Testing exercises remain valuable even after a written plan exists, since plans can become outdated or reveal gaps only when exercised (E is incorrect).

CompTIA logic: DR/BCP testing exercises exist on a spectrum of realism, cost, and risk: tabletop (discussion only, lowest cost/risk) β†’ simulation (more interactive walkthrough) β†’ parallel processing (recovery systems run alongside production) β†’ full interruption/failover (production actually cut over, highest realism and risk). Each type catches different kinds of gaps.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Tabletop is discussion-based; parallel processing runs recovery systems alongside production.

questions.question: Following a major outage affecting an organization's entire data center, the recovery team must decide which systems to bring back online first. According to standard disaster recovery planning principles, which factor should PRIMARILY drive the order in which systems are restored?

options.text: The criticality of each system to business operations, often informed by business impact analysis, with the most critical systems restored first
The order in which systems happen to be physically racked in the data center
The alphabetical order of system hostnames
Restoring the least critical systems first so that staff can practice on lower-stakes systems before tackling critical ones

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Restoration order should follow each system's criticality to the business, usually determined by the business impact analysis and RTOs, so the most critical systems return first. Physical rack order (B) and alphabetical hostnames (C) have no relationship to business priority. Restoring the least critical systems first (D) leaves the most important functions offline longest and increases overall impact.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Restoration order should follow business criticality from the BIA. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A data center design requires the highest level of resilience against power-related outages. Which combination of power measures provides the GREATEST protection?

options.text: A single utility feed with a very large UPS system
Dual utility feeds from separate substations, plus an on-site generator and UPS
A battery backup system only, without a generator or dual utility feeds
A generator alone without UPS to save cost

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Dual utility feeds from separate substations, plus a UPS for instant bridging and a generator for extended outages, remove every power single point of failure. A single feed with a large UPS (A) still depends on one utility and batteries eventually run out. Battery backup only (C) cannot sustain a prolonged outage. A generator alone (D) leaves a gap while it starts, causing an interruption.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Dual substation feeds plus generator and UPS remove power single points of failure. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A government agency requires that all data remain within government-controlled facilities, that no resources be shared with any other organization, and that the agency maintain direct physical control over all hardware. Which cloud deployment model satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Community cloud — shared among organizations with common interests such as government agencies
Public cloud — infrastructure shared among multiple tenants managed by a CSP
Hybrid cloud — combination of on-premises and public cloud resources
Private cloud — dedicated infrastructure operated solely for one organization

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. A private cloud is dedicated to one organization and can be hosted in its own facilities, meeting the requirements of no sharing and direct physical control. A community cloud (A) is shared by several organizations, even if they have common missions. A public cloud (B) is multi-tenant infrastructure run by a provider. A hybrid cloud (C) includes public cloud resources, violating the no-sharing requirement.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Dedicated single-tenant infrastructure under the agency control is a private cloud; options include give-away descriptions. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A healthcare organization requires that patient records be encrypted while stored in an S3 bucket, encrypted when being transmitted over the internet, and also encrypted while being processed in memory by the analytics application. Which combination of data states is being addressed?

options.text: Data in transit, data in use, and data sovereignty
Data at rest, data in transit, and data in use
Data masking, data tokenization, and data archival
Data at rest, data in transit, and data classification

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Records stored in S3 are data at rest, records sent over the internet are data in transit, and records processed in memory by the application are data in use; these are the three data states. Option A replaces data at rest with data sovereignty, which is a legal concept. Option C lists protection techniques and archival, not states. Option D includes data classification, which is a labeling process, not a state.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - S3 storage, internet transmission and in-memory processing are at rest, in transit and in use. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A hospital wants to ensure that a patient's medical records can only be viewed by clinicians who are currently assigned to that patient's care team, with access automatically granted or revoked based on attributes such as department, shift schedule, and current patient assignments, rather than a fixed job-title-based role. Which access control model BEST meets this requirement?
tags: Identity and Access Management - Access Control Models
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Attribute-based access control evaluates attributes such as department, shift schedule and current patient assignment, granting or revoking access dynamically. DAC (A) lets resource owners grant access at their discretion. MAC (B) relies on fixed labels and clearances set centrally. RBAC (C) grants permissions based on a static job role and would not automatically follow per-patient care team assignments.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Access driven by department, shift and patient assignment attributes is ABAC. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An administrator wants to reduce email spoofing of the company's domain by (1) specifying which mail servers are authorized to send email on behalf of the domain and (2) digitally signing outgoing messages so recipients can verify the message content was not altered in transit. Which TWO email security protocols should be implemented to achieve these two goals? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance (DMARC)

questions.justification:
SPF publishes a DNS record listing the mail servers authorized to send email for a domain, directly addressing the first goal. DKIM adds a cryptographic signature to outgoing messages, allowing recipients to verify that the message content has not been altered, directly addressing the second goal. DMARC (C) builds on SPF and DKIM to define a policy for handling messages that fail those checks, but it does not itself perform sender authorization or message signing. IMAP (D) and POP3 (E) are email retrieval protocols unrelated to anti-spoofing.

CompTIA logic: DMARC is closely associated with anti-spoofing and is often the first answer candidates think of, but DMARC is a policy/reporting layer that relies on the results of SPF and DKIM rather than performing the authorization or signing itself. When a question describes the two underlying mechanisms (authorized senders and message signing) rather than the reporting policy, SPF and DKIM are the correct pair.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - SPF authorizes sending servers and DKIM signs messages.

questions.question: A security team documents the standard, approved configuration settings, including installed software, open ports, and security settings, that all newly deployed workstations must match before being placed into production. This documented standard configuration is known as a:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. A secure baseline is the documented, approved configuration (software, ports, security settings) that every new workstation must match, and it is the reference for detecting drift. A penetration test (B) actively tries to exploit weaknesses. A CIS Benchmark compliance assessment profile (C) is a tool or reference that can inform or measure a baseline, but it is not the organization's own documented standard. A vulnerability scan (D) identifies known weaknesses rather than defining the configuration.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A documented standard configuration for new systems is a secure baseline. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization is upgrading its wireless network and wants to use the most current Wi-Fi security standard, which provides stronger encryption and protects against offline dictionary attacks on captured handshakes compared to its predecessor. Which wireless security standard should the organization implement?

options.text: WPA2-Enterprise using EAP-TTLS with certificate-based authentication

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. WPA3 is the current Wi-Fi security standard; its SAE (Simultaneous Authentication of Equals) handshake resists offline dictionary attacks on captured handshakes and it adds stronger encryption. WPA (A) is an outdated interim standard. WPA2 (B), in its personal mode, is vulnerable to offline dictionary attacks on the captured 4-way handshake. WPA2-Enterprise with EAP-TTLS (C) is a strong configuration, but it is still the predecessor standard rather than the most current one.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - WPA3 (SAE) is the current standard and resists offline dictionary attacks. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A company issues corporate smartphones to its sales team, who frequently access company email and customer data while traveling. Which TWO of the following mobile device hardening techniques would BEST protect company data if a device is lost or stolen? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Enabling biometric authentication as the sole unlock method, removing the PIN requirement
Enrolling the device in a mobile application management (MAM) solution to control app access
Deploying a VPN client configured to route all corporate traffic through headquarters

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A, C. Full device encryption keeps data unreadable without the unlock credentials, and remote wipe lets the organization erase a lost or stolen phone. Using biometrics as the only unlock method and removing the PIN (B) weakens authentication and fallback control. MAM (D) manages corporate apps and can help with selective wipe, but on its own does not protect all data at rest on a lost device. A full-tunnel VPN (E) protects data in transit, not data stored on the device.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Full device encryption and remote wipe protect data on lost or stolen phones. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question:
A security architect at a manufacturing company is conducting a network security review of the operational technology (OT) environment. The factory floor runs 47 IoT sensors embedded in CNC machines and conveyor systems, monitoring temperature, vibration, and cycle counts in real time. The devices run a proprietary RTOS with no support for third-party software installation, 32 MB of RAM, no local encryption capability, and firmware update cycles averaging 18 months. The OEM's support contract expired two years ago, meaning patches for known CVEs are no longer being released. The devices currently share the same flat network as corporate workstations and the ERP system. The architect must recommend the single most impactful control to reduce the risk these devices pose to the broader corporate network without requiring changes to the devices themselves.

Given these constraints, which of the following is the MOST appropriate way to reduce the risk these devices pose to the rest of the network?

options.text: Install a full endpoint detection and response (EDR) agent on each device
Place the devices on an isolated network segment with restricted access to and from other systems
Apply vendor-provided firmware updates directly to production devices without staging or rollback testing
Require the devices to use the same VLAN as corporate workstations for easier management

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. The sensors cannot run agents, receive patches or encrypt data, so isolating them on a restricted network segment is the most impactful compensating control and requires no device changes. An EDR agent (A) cannot be installed on a proprietary RTOS with 32 MB of RAM. Applying firmware directly to production without staging (C) is risky and no patches are being released anyway. Keeping them on the corporate workstation VLAN (D) preserves the flat network that creates the risk.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Devices that cannot be hardened should be isolated on a restricted segment. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A web application developer wants to ensure that data submitted through a web form, such as a username field, cannot be used to inject malicious script code that executes in other users' browsers when the data is later displayed on a page. Which security technique addresses this risk?

options.text: Setting the Secure attribute on cookies
Enabling full disk encryption on the web server

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Input validation restricts submissions to expected formats, and output encoding renders stored data as text instead of executable markup, which prevents cross-site scripting. The Secure cookie attribute (A) only ensures cookies travel over HTTPS. Full disk encryption (B) protects data at rest on the server and does nothing about script injection. A longer session timeout (D) is unrelated and increases exposure if a session is hijacked.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Input validation and output encoding mitigate XSS. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization maintains a centralized database that tracks every laptop, server, and mobile device it owns, including the assigned user, physical location, purchase date, and warranty status. This practice is BEST described as:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Tracking every owned device with its assigned user, location, purchase date and warranty is asset inventory management, which underpins patching, accountability and disposal. Incident response (A) handles security events after they occur. Penetration testing (C) simulates attacks to test defenses. Vulnerability scanning (D) identifies weaknesses in systems. None of these maintain a record of organizational assets. Key takeaway: the details in this scenario point to Asset inventory management.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A database tracking owned devices, users and locations is asset inventory management. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization is decommissioning a batch of old laptops that contained sensitive employee records. Which TWO of the following actions should be performed as part of secure asset disposal? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Perform data sanitization on the storage drives before disposal
Encrypt the drives with BitLocker prior to donating the devices to charity, without performing a full wipe
Document the disposal process, including certificates of destruction where applicable
Transfer devices to a certified electronics recycler under a standard terms-of-service agreement, without requesting a certificate of destruction
Reimage the laptops with a clean OS installation, treating the reimage as equivalent to a NIST-compliant data sanitization

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A, C. Secure disposal requires sanitizing the drives (wiping, degaussing, cryptographic erase or destruction) and documenting the process, including certificates of destruction, for audit purposes. Encrypting with BitLocker without wiping before donation (B) leaves the data and possibly keys in place. Handing devices to a recycler without requesting a certificate of destruction (D) removes the audit trail. Reimaging with a clean OS (E) is not equivalent to NIST-compliant sanitization; data may remain recoverable.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Sanitize drives and document disposal with certificates of destruction. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization's data retention policy states that email records should be deleted after three years. However, the legal department notifies IT that the company is involved in pending litigation and that all emails related to a specific project, regardless of age, must be preserved and must not be deleted until the litigation concludes. Which concept BEST describes the legal department's instruction?
tags: Asset Management - Legal Hold vs Retention Policy
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. A legal hold requires preserving data relevant to pending or anticipated litigation and overrides normal retention and deletion schedules until it is lifted. The right to be forgotten (A) is an individual's request to delete personal data, the opposite of preservation. Data minimization (B) limits collection and retention to what is necessary. Data sovereignty (D) concerns which jurisdiction's laws apply to stored data.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Preserving data for pending litigation despite retention rules is a legal hold. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A security team runs a vulnerability scan using an account with valid login credentials on the target systems, allowing the scanner to check installed software versions, configuration settings, and local security policies in addition to network-facing services. This type of scan is known as a:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. A credentialed scan logs into targets with valid accounts, so it can inspect installed software versions, configuration settings and local policies, giving more accurate results. A non-credentialed scan (B) sees only externally exposed services and tends to produce more false positives. A packet capture (C) records network traffic. A penetration test (D) goes further by actively exploiting vulnerabilities.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - A scan authenticating with valid credentials is a credentialed scan. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A vulnerability scanner assigns a score of 9.8 to a discovered flaw in a web server, indicating it is critical and should be patched immediately. The score uses a standardized, vendor-neutral framework. Which framework provides this numerical severity scoring?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. The Common Vulnerability Scoring System is the vendor-neutral framework that rates severity from 0.0 to 10.0 based on exploitability and impact; 9.8 is critical. CVE (A) is the identifier catalog for publicly known vulnerabilities, not a score. The NVD (B) publishes CVE entries enriched with CVSS scores but is a database. SCAP (C) is a suite of automation standards that includes CVSS, not the scoring system itself.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - CVSS provides the 0-10 severity score. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are typical activities within the vulnerability management process? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Scanning systems to identify known vulnerabilities
Apply every available patch within 24 hours of release, bypassing normal change management and testing procedures
Prioritizing and remediating identified vulnerabilities based on risk
Categorise all discovered vulnerabilities as low risk in the tracking tool to reduce the remediation backlog
Delegate all vulnerability remediation decisions to individual system owners with no centralised tracking or SLA requirements

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A, C. Vulnerability management is a cycle of identifying vulnerabilities through scanning and then prioritizing and remediating them based on risk. Applying every patch within 24 hours while bypassing change management and testing (B) risks outages and is not standard practice. Marking all findings as low risk to shrink the backlog (D) falsifies risk. Delegating everything to owners with no central tracking or SLAs (E) removes oversight and accountability.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Scanning and risk-based prioritization/remediation are core vulnerability management activities. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question:
A vulnerability scan flags a web server as running a version of software with a known critical vulnerability. However, upon investigation, the security analyst discovers that the vendor's patch for this vulnerability was already applied two weeks ago, and the scanner's vulnerability definitions had not yet been updated to reflect this.

This scan result is BEST described as a:
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. The scanner reported a vulnerability that no longer exists because the patch was applied and its definitions were outdated: a false positive. A false negative (A) is the opposite, a real vulnerability the scanner misses. A true positive (B) would mean the vulnerability genuinely exists. A zero-day (D) is a flaw unknown to the vendor with no patch, whereas this one was already patched.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Reporting a vulnerability that was already patched is a false positive. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A security analyst reviewing a vulnerability report sees a reference number in the format 'CVE-2024-12345' along with a severity score of 9.8 out of 10. Which statement BEST describes the relationship between these two pieces of information?

options.text: The CVE number is a unique identifier for the specific publicly known vulnerability, while the score of 9.8 is a CVSS rating describing its severity
The CVE number is the severity score, and 9.8 is the unique vulnerability identifier
Both numbers refer to the same scoring system and are interchangeable
The CVE number indicates how many systems are affected, and 9.8 indicates the patch version

questions.justification:
A CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) entry is a unique identifier assigned to a specific, publicly disclosed vulnerability, allowing it to be referenced consistently across tools and reports. CVSS (Common Vulnerability Scoring System) provides a numerical severity score, such as 9.8, based on factors like exploitability and impact. The two systems work together: the CVE identifies which vulnerability is being discussed, while the CVSS score indicates how severe it is. Options B, C, and D all incorrectly conflate or misattribute the purposes of these two distinct identifiers.

CompTIA logic: CVE and CVSS are easy to confuse because both appear together in vulnerability reports and both involve numbers. The key distinction is that CVE is an identifier (which vulnerability), while CVSS is a score (how severe). Remembering that CVE entries look like 'CVE-YEAR-NUMBER' while CVSS scores are always a number from 0.0 to 10.0 can help distinguish them quickly.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - CVE identifies the vulnerability; CVSS scores its severity.

questions.question: A security operations center (SOC) uses a platform that collects log data from firewalls, servers, and endpoints across the organization, correlates events from these different sources, and generates alerts when suspicious patterns are detected across multiple systems. This platform is BEST described as a:

options.text: Security information and event management (SIEM) system
Security orchestration, automation and response (SOAR) platform

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. A SIEM aggregates logs from firewalls, servers and endpoints, correlates events across sources and generates alerts on suspicious patterns. A VPN concentrator (A) terminates remote access tunnels. A load balancer (B) distributes traffic across servers. A SOAR platform (D) consumes alerts to orchestrate and automate response playbooks; it may integrate with a SIEM, but it is not the log collection and correlation platform described.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Collecting and correlating logs from many sources and alerting is a SIEM. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A network operations center receives real-time notifications from routers, switches, and UPS units about status changes such as interface failures or high temperature alerts. These notifications are sent from devices to a central management station automatically. Which protocol is used for these device status notifications?
questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. SNMP traps and informs are sent automatically by routers, switches and UPS units to a management station when status changes, such as an interface failure or temperature threshold. ICMP (A) is used for diagnostics such as ping. Syslog (B) forwards text log messages to a collector but is not the device management notification protocol. NetFlow (D) exports traffic flow metadata, not device health alerts.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Device-initiated status notifications (traps) use SNMP. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization configures all of its servers, network devices, and applications to forward their log data to a single centralized logging server, where the logs are stored, indexed, and made searchable for security analysts. Which of the following BEST describes the primary security benefit of this practice?

options.text: It provides real-time automated threat blocking by analysing log content against known attack signatures
It allows analysts to search and correlate events across multiple systems from a single location, which would be difficult if logs remained scattered across individual devices
It reduces each server individual storage requirements by offloading all log processing to the central appliance
It automatically remediates vulnerabilities discovered in the aggregated log stream before they can be exploited

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Centralizing logs lets analysts search and correlate events across many systems from one place, which is essential for detecting multi-system attack patterns. Real-time automated blocking (A) is the job of an IPS or SOAR, not a log server. Reducing local storage (C) is an operational side effect, not the primary security benefit. Centralized logs do not remediate vulnerabilities (D); they provide visibility.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Centralized logging lets analysts search and correlate events across systems. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A SOC analyst notices that a particular alert rule generates hundreds of alerts per day, the vast majority of which are determined to be benign after investigation, consuming significant analyst time. Which TWO of the following actions would help address this issue? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Tune the alert thresholds or criteria to reduce the number of benign alerts
Archive all triggered alerts automatically to long-term storage without analyst review to preserve potential evidence
Review and adjust the rule logic to better distinguish malicious activity from normal behavior
Escalate every alert generated by this rule to a senior analyst without any initial triage or suppression
Reduce logging verbosity on the monitored system to generate fewer raw log entries, indirectly lowering alert volume

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A, C. Tuning thresholds and refining rule logic to separate malicious from normal behavior reduces false positives and alert fatigue while keeping detection. Auto-archiving alerts without review (B) means real incidents could be missed. Escalating every alert to a senior analyst without triage (D) just moves the fatigue. Reducing logging verbosity (E) lowers alert volume by losing visibility, which harms detection and investigations.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Tuning thresholds and improving rule logic reduce false positives. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A company wants to prevent employees from accessing known malicious and inappropriate websites by blocking access based on the website's category, such as gambling or malware-hosting, before the connection is even established, regardless of which device or browser is used. Which technology is BEST suited for this purpose?

options.text: Network access control (NAC) with device posture assessment at network entry points
Web content proxy with agent-based URL inspection deployed on each endpoint

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. DNS filtering blocks resolution of domains in categories such as gambling or malware hosting, so the connection never starts, and it applies network-wide to any device or browser. NAC with posture assessment (A) controls which devices may join the network, not which sites they visit. An agent-based web proxy (B) depends on software installed on each endpoint, so it does not cover every device. A host-based firewall (D) filters connections per host and is not category-based web filtering.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Category-based blocking at name resolution for any device is DNS filtering. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: A security hardening checklist requires administrators to disable all unencrypted remote terminal access. An administrator confirms the service runs on TCP port 23. Which protocol must be disabled to comply with this requirement?
tags: Enterprise Security Capabilities - Disabling Unnecessary Protocols
questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Telnet provides unencrypted remote terminal access on TCP port 23, sending credentials in plaintext, so it must be disabled. RDP (B) is graphical remote desktop on port 3389 and is encrypted. SSH (C) on port 22 is the encrypted replacement for Telnet and should remain enabled. SFTP (D) provides encrypted file transfer over SSH, not a terminal on port 23.
questions.review_notes: SME review: correct - Unencrypted remote terminal on TCP 23 is Telnet. - Approved by SME editor.

questions.question: An organization replaces its traditional signature-based antivirus software with an endpoint detection and response (EDR) solution. Which TWO of the following capabilities does EDR typically add beyond traditional antivirus? (Choose TWO.)
tags: Enterprise Security Capabilities - EDR vs Antivirus

options.text: Continuous behavioral monitoring of endpoint activity to detect suspicious patterns, even from previously unknown threats
